News.title: Mystery over death of dad found with head injury on school field by girl, 11, after CCTV of final moments went dark
News.content:
DEATH RIDDLE Mystery over death of dad found with head injury on school field by girl, 11, after CCTV of final moments went dark

THE death of a dad found by an 11-year-old girl on a school field remains a mystery after CCTV of his final moments went dark, an inquest heard.

Neil Thompson, 45, was discovered at Smestow Academy in Wolverhampton on January 19 this year as the girl got ready to do PE.



An inquest heard he died from aspiration of blood caused by traumatic facial injuries and a traumatic head injury.

Police initially launched a homicide investigation but the hearing was told mystery still surrounds exactly how he came to sustain his fatal injuries.



The court heard Neil had left his home on an electric bike at around 8.17pm on January 18 to visit a friend.

He left at around 1am the next morning, with CCTV capturing the dad travelling along a canal towpath at 1.26am.



A member of the public walking his dog through Smestow Valley Nature Reserve photographed him in the school grounds at around 7.15am.

He was believed to still be alive at that point but what happened during the intervening hours remains unclear, the inquest was told.

A post-mortem found significant injuries to the left side of his face, evidence of a traumatic brain injury and a fracture around the left eye socket.

Neil had also suffered an injury to the front of his neck, the court was told.



Consultant pathologist Dr Brett Lockyer said the injuries were consistent with blunt-force trauma and suggested Neil could have suffered the injuries in a heavy fall but could have also been assaulted.

Giving evidence, West Midlands Police Detective Inspector Joe Davenport, who led the homicide investigation, said police carried out an extensive CCTV and forensic investigation.

The probe placed Neil on the canal towpath between approximately 1am and 1.26am but there was no CCTV showing how he suffered his injuries.



Det Insp Davenport said his own theory was that Neil may have been thrown from his bike while travelling at speed along the uneven towpath in poor weather conditions.

The inquest also heard there was no clear understanding of how Neil got from the towpath to the school playing field where his body was found.

He would have had to negotiate or scale a fence to enter the school grounds but investigators were unable to establish how or when he made that journey.

Police also found no confirmed damage or blood evidence along the towpath during their investigation.

CCTV from Smestow Academy and various access points to the nature reserve showed no evidence of another person with Neil on the canal towpath or around the school grounds at the relevant time.



Investigators also found no evidence he had been robbed.

But DI Davenport admitted the whole nature reserve could not be completely sealed off and therefore the possibility of another person being involved could not be entirely excluded.

Black Country Area Coroner Mrs Joanne Lees recorded a narrative conclusion.

She said Neil died from aspiration of blood caused by traumatic facial injuries and a traumatic head injury, with the circumstances in which those injuries were sustained unknown.

In a statement at the time of his death, Neil’s family said: “Our beautiful son, brother, father and friend Chuck, very much loved in the community of fishing, his one true love.



“His love for life and funny stories touched the lives of so many people.”

The dad of the 11-year-old girl who found the body told previously how she was left “really shaken up” after making the grim discovery.

He said: “My daughter phoned her mum up, screaming, and told her that she found a dead body by the goal posts on the field.

“She’s only 11 years of age. They went out for PE and it was very foggy.

“It’s terrible what she’s had to see.”

News.title: Track ‘defect’ found on rails where Lewes train crashed & left 30 injured – as questions mount over new CCTV evidence
News.content:
A TRACK “defect” was discovered on the railway line where the Lewes train crashed and left 30 people injures – as questions mount over new CCTV evidence.

Investigators have now released their initial report into Britain’s second rail derailment in two months after disaster struck last Thursday in East Sussex.



When the train set off from London Victoria – it was a journey like any other, with commuters heading home back into the Sussex countryside.

But the rear three carriages of the packed 2.24pm service to Eastbourne left the track around 90 minutes later in scenes of chaos.



A rail track defect existed in the area where the train left the tracks, it has now been revealed.

An interim report by the Rail Accident Investigation Branch (RAIB) said CCTV images from preceding services on the line show the fault, which it described as a “track geometry irregularity”.



The preliminary report also said there were “marks observed on the rails near the point of derailment” which are “consistent with the wheels of the derailed rear vehicles having climbed over the rails”.

It added there was “evidence of previous track maintenance activity” and investigators had received reports of “rough riding” at the location from passengers on other trains.



Preliminary analysis of the derailed train’s onboard data recorder show it was travelling at about 65mph as it approached the point of derailment in Lewes at 3.54pm on August 13.

About 150 people were onboard the eight-carriage Southern train with three carriages ending up on their side, trapping passengers.

A total of 30 people were injured, included 20 who required hospital treatment, the RAIB said.

The RAIB said its investigation will consider the weather conditions on August 13, which were hot and sunny, as well as the status of the track, embankment, condition of the train and the effectiveness of any measures taken to address potential issues caused by hot weather.

Network Rail and Greater Thameslink Railway said in a joint statement that they were “very sorry that this happened on our railway”.



“Our thoughts remain with everyone affected, especially those who were injured and the family and friends of those on board the train.

“We also recognise the ongoing impact the incident has had on customers, local communities and railway colleagues.

“Safety is and will always remain our highest priority. While Britain’s railway is one of the safest in the world, when incidents like this occur it is essential that we understand exactly what happened and identify any lessons that can be learned.”

They added they will “carefully consider any recommendations” from the investigation and work to implement them.



“Given the complexity of the issues being examined, it is important that the independent investigation is allowed to reach its conclusions.

“We will continue to cooperate fully with the RAIB throughout this process,” they added.

Last week’s derailment saw passengers tossed around inside the train with commuters describing people “dropping from the sky”.

The derailment left 40 of the train’s 150 terrified passengers trapped on one of the hottest days of the year.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Terrifying pictures from the scene showed the carriages lying on their sides, with passengers standing on top of the train as they were helped to safety.

One bloodied passenger described the moment everything went “topsy-turvy” as the train suddenly picked up speed and rolled over.

News.title: Human bones ‘unearthed by wildfires’ in UK beauty spot – as cops launch probe
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

GRISLY DISCOVERY Human bones ‘unearthed by wildfires’ in UK beauty spot – as cops launch probe

HUMAN bones have been unearthed in a popular beauty spot with cops treating it as a crime scene.

A probe is now underway to establish the age and identity of the remains.

Police were scrambled to the popular London park after the gruesome discovery was made.

Local residents claim fires at Bedfont Lakes Country Park in Bedfont, Hounslow unearthed the remains after two blazes in the last couple of weeks.





Fires burn away the topsoil which can reveal hidden items buried beneath.

This means the skeleton could be historical or modern – with a crime scene now in place.

A spokesperson from the Metropolitan Police told The Sun: “Police were called at 18:35hrs on Wednesday, 12 August to reports of bones being found at Bedfont Pits, Feltham.

“The bones were confirmed to be human and further testing is underway to establish the age of the bones and ascertain identity.



“An investigation is ongoing, and a crime scene remains in place.”

London Fire Brigade did not wish to comment when contacted by The Sun Online.

News.title: Cops hunt BMW driver walking on busy A-road after two children, 12 & 13, seriously injured in crash before he fled
News.content:
POLICE have released CCTV of a BMW driver who fled the scene after two children were seriously injured in a horror crash.

A black BMW reportedly crashed into two stationary cars on the A13 in Farnham, Surrey, on July 26 before the driver left on foot.



Emergency services raced to the road and two children, aged 12 and 13, were taken to hospital after sustaining serious injuries.

Police have released footage of the driver walking along the busy A-road after he left the scene.



Surrey Police said he is described as a Black man in his twenties, wearing a black Nike top, black shorts and a pair of sliders with no socks.

He was last seen fleeing through the undergrowth, heading towards Farnham town centre.



The force said: “Can you help us identify this man?

“We are looking to speak to him in connection with a serious collision in Farnham last month.

“Officers were called to the A31 Farnham Bypass on Sunday, 26 July at around 2.45pm following a collision involving three vehicles: a black BMW 3 series, a white Toyota Yaris, and a grey BMW 330.”

A spokesperson previously said: “It is reported that the driver of the black BMW collided with the other vehicles, both of which were stationary, and fled the scene on foot.



“Two children aged 12 and 13, who were passengers in one of the other vehicles, sustained serious injuries from the collision and were admitted to hospital.”

They continued: “Were you in the area around the A31 Farnham Bypass between 2.40pm and 2.50pm on Sunday, 26 July? Did you see or hear anything that you think we should know about?

“We are asking anyone who may have witnessed this collision, or who may have CCTV, dashcam, or helmet cam footage that may have captured all or part of this incident, to get in touch.”

News.title: Delivery driver avoids jail after blaming eating disorder for stealing £4k of weight-loss drug Ozempic from workplace
News.content:
JAB CLAIM Delivery driver avoids jail after blaming eating disorder for stealing £4k of weight-loss drug Ozempic from workplace

A DELIVERY driver who avoided jail after blaming an eating disorder for stealing £4,000 worth of Ozempic from his workplace.

Peter Daniel was handed a six-month sentence, suspended for 18 months, and was ordered to pay compensation after swiping more than 30 boxes of the weight-loss drug.

The 62-year-old previously had an unblemished 23-year record working for pharmaceutical giant Cencora Alliance Healthcare.



But he told cops he had taken the weight loss drugs to help treat the unspecified eating disorder.



His crimes only came to light when a customer complained that part of their order was missing.

When company bosses checked CCTV, they saw Daniel swiping boxes from pigeon holes that weren’t his.

He initially appeared at Croydon Magistrate’s Court in June accused of one count of theft by employee to which he pleaded guilty.

Mohammed Bismillah, defending, described his client as having a previously “unblemished record.”

“These items that were misappropriated were not for financial gain,” he said.

“He has an eating disorder and they were for his own use.”

Daniel was handed the suspended sentence, ordered to attend a mental health treatment programme for 18 months and given a rehabilitation activity requirement of 10 days.



Daniel, of Croydon, south London, began working for what is now Cencora Alliance Healthcare in 2002, according to his LinkedIn account.

The thefts were all said to have taken place between April 17 and May 5 this year, with the customer making the complaint on May 13.

Michael A’Herne, prosecuting, said: “The complainant in this matter drove medication to various pharmacies such as Boots and others.

“On May 13, a customer said they were missing refrigeration materials and therefore CCTV was checked.

“The defendant stated that in his role as a delivery driver he would collect packs from his pigeon hole but on CCTV he could be seen to swipe several products from several different pigeon holes.



“Police searched his address. They looked in his fridge and found 34 Ozempic boxes.

“These could be dangerous in the hands of someone who doesn’t know how to use them or has not been prescribed them.”

The 34 Ozempic boxes were worth £4,080.

Mr A’Herne went on to reveal that the company has up to 15,000 missing parcels a month, costing £300,000.

“I believe that the defendant had some contribution to those figures,” he added.



Daniel has five previous convictions, the court heard, although all were from before 1991.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“He worked for the company for 23 years and breached a high degree of trust – he was trusted to deliver those items,” Mr A’Herne added.

Daniel was also ordered to pay costs to the Crown Prosecution Service of £85, a surcharge of £154 and compensation to his employer of £4,080 to cover the cost of the drugs.

News.title: Cops launch double murder probe as two men found dead in Glasgow flat named
News.content:
A DOUBLE murder probe has been launched after two men were found dead in a flat in Glasgow’s west end.

Paul Lafferty, 50, and Gary Beaton 54, were discovered fatally wounded in the home in Chancellor Street in the city’s Partick on Sunday afternoon.



They were pronounced dead at the scene.

Following post-mortems, police are now treating their deaths as murder.





Both families of the men have been made aware and are being support by specialist officers.

Senior investigating officer Detective Superintendent Cheryl Kelly, of the Major Investigation Team, said: “My thoughts are with the families of Paul and Gary at this extremely difficult time and we are doing all we can to get them answers.

“Our investigation into the deaths of Paul and Gary are continuing and I would urgently appeal to anyone with information who has not already spoken with us to please do so.

“It is vital we trace whoever is responsible and we are fully committed to doing this.



“A significant amount of resources have been dedicated to this investigation and there will be a large police presence in the area as these enquiries continue.

“I am appealing directly to anyone with any information, no matter how small or insignificant they feel it may be, should come forward and speak to us. Please do not assume that the police already know the information you have.

“We are keen to hear from anyone who knew Paul and Gary or who were in the Partick area, near to Chancellor Street from Friday morning from 9am on 14 August, 2026, who seen Paul or Gary or seen or heard anything suspicious.

Superintendent Craig Brady said: “I would like to extend my sympathies to the family and friends of Paul and Gary as they try to come to terms with their loss.

“We understand the significant impact this will have on the local community and I would like to thank everyone for their help so far.



“High visibility patrols remain in the area and there will be an increased police presence as the investigation continues.

“If anyone has any concerns, or information, please speak to officers.”

Forensic teams have been coming and going from the property for days as detectives work to establish exactly what happened.

They have been seen searching drains and trees on the street as part of the major investigation.

At least six officers, including CID detectives, were seen at the scene, with a number of police cars parked in surrounding streets.



Up to 10 police cars and two ambulances were reported at the scene.

News.title: Record 1.3m foreign migrants claiming UK benefits as Reform vows total ban on handouts
News.content:
A RECORD 1.3million migrants are claiming benefits in the UK, according to government figures.

Reform UK has recently vowed a total ban on the handouts for foreign nationals, who account for over a third of Universal Credit (UC) claims.



Data released by the Department for Work and Pensioners revealed almost 1.3 million migrants were claiming UC in May 2026.

The staggering figure is up 20,000 from the previous year, with EU citizens making up half of the total foreign claimants.



Asylum seekers who have been granted refugee status and migrants with indefinite leave to remain or settled status are eligible for the handouts.

But Reform UK has recently proposed a major shake-up of the welfare system, which it slammed as “plain immoral”.



Nigel Farage‘s party previously outlined its plans to stop foreign nationals claiming Universal Credit.

And proposals also extend to housing benefit, pension credit, child benefit, jobseekers’ allowance, disability benefits and free childcare.

Treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick said the changes could save the Treasury some £50billion a year.

Mr Jenrick pointed to Britain’s soaring welfare bill, which is set to hit £407billion within the next four years.



In a speech on Monday, he said: “Forcing British workers to pay for the benefits of foreigners is not just economically illiterate but plain immoral.

“British taxpayers cannot afford to subsidise everyone on the planet, especially those who have not paid in.

“The public have been crying out for this change for decades.”

But the plans would mean renegotiating the Brexit deal with Brussels as the ban would also include EU citizens with settled status.

Labour has blasted Reform’s plan, saying it would “plunge the UK back into years of Brexit negotiations”.



A spokesman added it will “strip support from potentially millions of people who have lawfully lived, worked and paid taxes in Britain for years”.

It comes as UC claimants across the UK skyrocketed again to a record high of 8.4million.

The shocking figure is up 700,000 from the same time last year, despite Labour’s pledge to “get Brits working”.

It means the number of claimants is now at the highest level it has been since the introduction of Universal Credit (UC) in 2013.

But while the benefits caseload across the country has spiralled, the share of claimants in work has worryingly dropped.



Just 3.1million claimants were in employment in April 2026, which is just over a third (37.7 per cent) of all people on UC.

A year earlier, 3.2 million were employed, making up 41.9 per cent of the total figure.

Meanwhile, those in the “no work requirements” category has increased to more than half (51 per cent).

A DWP spokesperson said: “People who do not hold immigration status in the UK are unable to claim Universal Credit, and in the year to May, 84.5% of claimants were British or Irish nationals or had a right to abode.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Last November, we set out reforms to double the standard qualifying period to 10 years for most migrants, with shorter routes for those who contribute most to the UK.



“These reforms will ensure the right to live here permanently is earned. It is right that we support people who have lived here, worked and contributed for years, and then require support.”

News.title: Cops release new CCTV of car in desperate search for missing woman, 57, who suddenly left her home nearly a month ago
News.content:
FIND TRACEY Cops release new CCTV of car in desperate search for missing woman, 57, who suddenly left her home nearly a month ago

A WOMAN has been missing for almost a month as police release new images of her driving her car the morning she dissapeared.

Tracey Smith, 57, vanished on July 24 after she was last seen leaving her home in North Yorkshire in her black Fiat Panda.



North Yorkshire Police said her car could be in popular hiking areas and have asked runners and climbers to “keep an eye out”.

Detectives believe tracking her car will reveal more about Tracey’s movements.



Their enquiries have uncovered images of Tracey driving away from her home in Stokesley, North Yorkshire, on the day she disappeared.

Her car’s registration is WR10 ETK.

Officers believe it could be in the Cleveland and North Yorkshire border area or around the North York Moors and Cleveland Hills.

They are now calling on the “outdoor community” to help track it down.



Walkers, runners, hikers, cyclists, climbers and anyone else visiting the area have been asked to look out for the Fiat, including at beauty spots and in more remote locations.

Tracey is described as 5ft 5ins tall, of slim build, with shoulder-length blonde hair and a mole above her lip.

Investigators have not ruled out the possibility that she may have travelled to London, but finding her car remains a key focus of the search.

Inspector Ciaran Conlon, of Hambleton & Richmond Neighbourhood Policing Team, said: “Extensive enquiries are ongoing to help find Tracey whose disappearance continues to be of great concern to us and her friends and family.

“Finding her black Fiat Panda is one of the key priorities in our search and I appeal to everyone who enjoys the local area to keep an eye out for it – from local beauty spots to the more remote areas of the national park.



“I also make a direct appeal to Tracey – if you see or hear this appeal, please get in touch with the police, your family or friends, and let us know that you are safe.

“Or, if you prefer, you can contact the charity, missing people on their free and confidential helpline 116 000, who can pass on a message to help put people’s minds at rest.”

News.title: Kenya helicopter crash - latest: 6 dead as safari 'tourist' chopper crashes in Samburu
News.content:
Six people have been killed after a safari helicopter crashed near Mt Ololokwe in Kenya’s Samburu County, with tourists reportedly on board

A helicopter has crashed near Kirish close to Mt Ololokwe in Kenya’s Samburu County, with all six people on board dead.

A preliminary police report cited by Kenyan newspaper The Star suggested tourists were travelling in the aircraft, although their nationalities have not yet been established and this has not been confirmed.

Local residents and rescue teams were heading towards the scene, where smoke and fire had been seen following the crash.

The Kenya Civil Aviation Authority said the helicopter had been travelling towards the Ewaso Nyiro river, which runs through the Samburu National Reserve, shortly after 9am local time.

The helicopter was operated by local safari company Tropic Air and crashed in the foothills Mt Ololokwe, local media reports.

News.title: Shoreham deaths - latest: Child 'caught in fishing net' before three pulled from sea
News.content:
Three members of the same family died after getting into difficulty in the water at Shoreham-by-Sea in Sussex - while a young girl from the family is now fighting for her life

Eyewitnesses claim one of the children involved in a tragic incident in the water off Shoreham-by-Sea had become trapped in a fishing net.

Three people from the same family - a man, a woman, and a teenage girl - have died after getting into trouble in the sea sparking a massive emergency services response.

A fourth person, a younger girl from the same family, also got into difficulty but was pulled from the sea and remains in a critical condition in hospital. Local landscaper Joe Chrisp, 24, said: "It happened when I was on my way back from work. There were loads of police, and I got turned around. It’s so tragic. One of the kids apparently got caught in a fishing net."

Coastguard helicopters, ambulances and police were scrambled to the town in West Sussex on Tuesday afternoon following reports that four people were in trouble in the water. It's thought the family were camping near the scene and had entered the water for a group swim in the harbour, Sussex Police said.

People living in the area say Shoreham Harbour has a steep shelf, where the seabed drops away quickly. It can make it difficult for swimmers to keep their balance, they say. Prime Minister Andy Burnham called the incident "a real tragedy" and said there is more that can be done to prevent drowning deaths.

The tragic deaths in Shoreham today come as the Mirror has launched the Save Lives For Sam water safety campaign to tackle the UK's growing drowning crisis. Find out more about the campaign and how you can support it here.

News.title: How to beat price rises from energy bills to your mortgage - as inflation hits 2.9%
News.content:
Inflation has jumped to its highest rate since March - but there are plenty of ways you can fight back against price rises.

The Consumer Prices Index (CPI) measure of inflation rose to 2.9% in July, up from 2.6% in June. The increase was widely expected after energy bills jumped by 13% last month.

From energy bills to your mortgage, we explain all the ways to bring your bills down - plus a warning for savers, who may not be getting the most for their money.

View 5 Images Energy bills have been blamed for pushing up inflation (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

‌



Energy bills

The price of gas and electricity is set to rise again this winter. Energy analysts at Cornwall Insight are expecting another 4% jump in the Ofgem price cap from October. This would follow a 13% increase that already came into effect in July.

But experts at Uswitch.com say households can save money by switching to a fixed energy deal - with the best deals on the market currently undercutting the latest price cap prediction by around 12%.

Richard Neudegg, director of regulation at Uswitch.com, said: “Don’t suffer higher winter bills when you don’t have to – a decent fixed tariff beats these rates and protects you from further price rises. Every week spent on a standard tariff is another week paying higher rates than you need to.”

You can also save money by getting your home ready for winter, by sealing any window or door drafts and bleeding radiators, and checking if you are entitled to any energy help. For example, Winter Fuel Payments are worth up to £300 and are available to those who are over state pension age. There is also the Warm Home Discount, which gives you £150 off your electricity bill if you claim certain benefits.

‌



Get the best deals and tips from Mirror Money WHATSAPP GROUP: Get money news and top deals straight to your phone by joining our Money WhatsApp group here. We also treat our community members to special offers, promotions, and adverts from us and our partners. If you don’t like our community, you can check out any time you like. If you’re curious, you can read our Privacy Notice. NEWSLETTER: Or sign up to the Mirror's Money newsletter here for all the best advice and shopping deals straight to your inbox.

Savings

Savers are being urged to check the rate they are getting on their savings, as around four in five accounts still pay above inflation, according to Moneyfacts. Its analysis shows there are currently 1,850 savings accounts that beat inflation. The top-paying easy-access account offers a rate of 5% - so if you saved £10,000 for one year, this would accrue £500 in interest. The real gains after inflation on this would be £210.

Caitlyn Eastell, Personal Finance Analyst at Moneyfacts, said: "For savers, beating inflation is the difference between simply earning interest and increasing the spending power of their money. While a balance can be growing on paper, it could be shrinking in value if the savings rate fails to keep pace with rising prices."

But those with larger savings pots also need to be aware of potential tax implications. Basic-rate taxpayers can earn up to £1,000 in savings interest each tax year before they start to pay tax on the interest earned. Higher rate taxpayers can earn up to £500 in savings interest before they have to pay tax, while additional rate taxpayers do not receive any allowance. Any interest earned above these limits is taxed at your usual income tax rate.

‌



Ms Eastell added: "Higher-rate taxpayer can use up their £500 Personal Savings Allowance with just £10,000 earning 5%, meaning any further interest could become taxable. Despite their slightly lower rates, this is where ISAs could become particularly valuable."

View 5 Images Check your savings are getting you the best returns (Image: Getty Images/Image Source)

Mortgage

Mortgage rates have risen since the start of the Iran war, although lenders have reversed some of those increases in recent weeks. But experts say the market remains volatile and it would be "impossible to rule out more yo-yoing" in mortgage rates.

If your current mortgage is expiring, remortgaging to a cheaper deal will save you money. You can lock into a new fixed deal normally three to six months before your current mortgage expires.

‌



To do this, you will need all the relevant information about your existing deal - such as the rate you are on and your loan to value (LTV). This is the amount you are borrowing compared to the property's value.

You can see what other deals are available to you by using an online comparison tool, or by speaking to a mortgage broker, as they will often have access to deals that aren't available on the open market.

You should also speak to your current lender to see what rates it can offer you. This is known as a product transfers, which is where you get a new deal from the same lender.

David Hollingworth, associate director at L&C Mortgages said: “The good news is that, because today’s increase in inflation was widely anticipated, it’s less likely for there to be big repercussions in markets that would put more pressure on lenders funding costs in the short term.

‌



"For anyone considering a purchase or remortgage, securing advice early remains important. Mortgage rates continue to change frequently, and the uncertain economic landscape will continue to dictate lender movements over the coming weeks.”

View 5 Images See if you can get a better deal on your broadband and mobile (Image: Getty Images)

Mobile and broadband

Mobile and broadband are widely considered to be essential services - but that doesn't mean you cannot save money. If you are out of contract, look at prices elsewhere using a comparison website to see what other deals are available. If you find a cheaper deal, you can either switch to this - or try asking your existing provider if it can give you a better price.

When comparing prices, look at how many minutes, texts and how much data you currently use, so you can find similar plans that suit your needs.

‌



For broadband, look at your current speed and if you need this fast of a deal. You may find you're actually paying too much right now for allowances or speeds you're not using.

Sarah Coles, head of personal finance at AJ Bell, said: "Broadband and media deals can be switched, or you may be able to call your provider and negotiate a better deal just by threatening to quit."

Water bills

Millions of households are set to pay even higher bills after it was confirmed last week that five water companies including debt-stricken Thames Water were provisionally allowed to hike costs. Ofwat had already previously allowed water firms to raise average bills by £157, or roughly 36%, by 2030.

But while you can't switch water providers, there are still ways to cut your costs. Every water company has a social tariff for eligible customers on a low income. Last year, almost two million households received support through social tariffs, with bills reduced by an average of £190.

‌



Sebrina McCullough, director of external relations at Money Wellness, said: “The rules are different depending on which water company you're with, so it's worth checking rather than assuming you won't qualify. If you're on a low income or your circumstances have changed, don't just carry on paying the full bill without checking.”

If you have more or the same number of bedrooms in your house than people, you may also be able to save money by getting a water meter.

It is also worth checking for free water-saving devices through Save Water Save Money. It varies depending on where you live, but some freebies include shower heads that regulate the flow of water, or tap inserts.

View 5 Images There are lots of ways to cut the cost of your supermarket shop (Image: coldsnowstorm/Getty)

‌



Food

Food inflation fell to 1.2% in July - the lowest level since September 2021. However, food producers warned earlier this week that soaring temperatures and droughts across the UK and Europe could drive prices higher.

Dr Liliana Danila, chief economist at the Food and Drink Federation, said: "Competition for fewer resources will in turn push up the price of ingredients for manufacturers.

"The UK's food and drink manufacturers work hard to absorb costs where they can, but are already grappling with rising costs as a result of war in Ukraine and in Iran, so we expect the additional upward pressure of reduced crops will be reflected in retail prices into next year."

Thankfully, there are plenty of ways to save money in the supermarkets. One of the most popular ways to save cash is yellow stickers and the best time for these discounts is typically toward the end of the day, although this does vary between stores. You could also try the Downshift Challenge, which is where you swap branded goods for supermarket-own. Depending on what you buy, you could save around 30% on your food bill.

‌



It also pays to compare prices using sites such as Trolley.co.uk which takes into account live prices across all the major supermarkets and other popular retailers. Other tips include being organised. By writing a shopping list and sticking to it, you will reduce impulse buys when you're in the store.

Finally, use your freezer to avoid throwing away food that can be eaten at a later date. You can tell if food can be frozen by checking product packaging for freezing instructions.

Train tickets

Train passengers face a potential 4.2% increase in ticket prices next year, based on inflation figures from today. The Retail Price Index (RPI) measure of inflation for July was also announced this morning and was confirmed to be 3.2%. Last year, rail increases were measured based on RPI in July plus one percentage point.

If this same method is used again, it would mean train tickets could jump by up to 4.2%. The Government has not confirmed if the price of train tickets will rise next year. Regulated train fares did not go up this year after the former Chancellor Rachel Reeves announced a price freeze.

‌



To save money on train fares, plan your journey as far in advance as possible to get discounted fares. Train companies typically release cheap advance tickets about 12 weeks ahead of the date of travel.

Split ticketing, which involves splitting your journey up into different sections, so you're buying lots of multiple tickets instead of just one single ticket, could also save you money.

For regular travellers, a railcard can save you between 30% and 50% off the price of your fare. You may also benefit from purchasing a season ticket or flexi ticket, again, depending on how often you travel.

Catherine Lyver from Railcard.co.uk said: "Brits are proving that saving money doesn't mean missing out. For many, the money saved with a Railcard becomes the ice cream, coffee or extra treat that makes a day out feel special."

News.title: Tear up 'damaging' migration plans or social care shake-up will fail, Burnham warned
News.content:
Tear up 'damaging' migration plans or social care shake-up will fail, Burnham warned

Analysis by trade union Unison revealed a sharp fall in overseas care workers being appointed, while the sector has a shortfall of nearly 100,000

View 3 Images New analysis reveals stark shortages in the social care sector (Image: Getty Images)

Andy Burnham's drive to sort out the social care crisis will fail if controversial immigration changes are pushed through, the PM has been warned.

‌



Unison says the number of international recruits into the sector has plummeted by more than two thirds in just a year - while jobs filled by British workers also fell. The Labour-affiliated union has written to Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood urging her to tear up plans to treble the time those on care worker visas have to wait before applying for permanent settlement.

‌



It warns the measure will cause "chaos and irreparable damage" to a sector which is already struggling. General secretary Andrea Egan said: “If the government’s serious about fixing social care, it should immediately scrap these cruel plans that will make it harder to recruit staff.

‌



"Terrible pay and working conditions are creating shortages in the social care sector. These figures make that crystal clear. A massive drop in overseas workers has not led to rising domestic recruitment or higher wages.

Reform civil war erupts as top supporter suspended after scathing Farage and Yusuf criticism READ MORE :

View 3 Images Unison chief Andrea Egan said the government's migration plans threaten Andy Burnham's social care shake-up (Image: Philip Coburn/Daily Mirror)

"Attempts to force existing staff out of the country are wrong by every measure. If the government doesn’t drop these plans, the prime minister’s hope of transforming the lives of millions through a national care service will never happen.”

‌



Analysis by Unison found the number of new international recruits into the care sector dropped from 105,000 in 2023/24 to 30,000 in 2025/26. At the sime time the number of social care jobs filled by British workers fell by 70,000.

And there are an estimated 96,000 vacancies across the sector, it said. The trade union has written to Ms Mahmood saying proposed changes to indefinite leave to remain (ILR) rules will worsen the shortage - and branded proposed rule changes morally wrong.

Controversial plans would see the standard rate for care workers' settlement rise from its current five years to 15. The Home Secretary said the existing rules are unfair and the right to remain in the UK must be earned.

‌



But there are growing calls for a carve-out for care workers, as the rules would apply to people already in the country. Last week borders minister Anna Turley told The Mirror: "I know the Home Secretary has done a huge amount of work on this, she's continuing to look at it at the moment, and I think these the policy will be developed over the coming months.

View 3 Images Borders minister Anna Turley said rules for migrant care workers are being looked at

"I know the Home Secretary will continue to look at that. I've heard myself many representations, people say particularly those working in the care sector. I know the Home Secretary is working at pace to make sure that we have a system that is fair, that recognises people's contribution, people who want to come to this country and work and work in our essential services and and and contribute.

‌



"But balance with the reality that we also have to make sure that we can have a sustainable social system, a welfare system that that British people can afford."

Mr Burnham has said he is prepared to use any political capital he can muster to sorting out Britain's care crisis. Last month he said he does not want to leave office without bringing about substantial change.

The Prime Minister - whose father Roy receives care for Alzheimer's - said: "I will go as quickly as I can on the reform of social care... I think there are major changes you can make before the next election.

‌



"This costs the NHS billions of pounds and we will never get the NHS back to good waiting time standards until we fix social care."

An independent review into the state of the care sector, being carried out by Baroness Louise Casey, has been accelerated to report back next year.

A government spokeswoman said: “The Prime Minister has set out his plan to start to mend our broken social care system based on a better deal with its workforce – with better progression, pay, training and job security at its heart.

Article continues below

“A consultation on elements of our earned settlement reforms has now closed, and we will set out our response in due course.”

News.title: Hayden Panettiere dies aged 36: Ex Brian Hickerson at scene when she died as mum breaks silence
News.content:
Hayden Panettiere has died at the age of 36, with the initial investigation from police finding there was 'no foul play' and autopsy results confirming 'no signs of trauma'

US actress Hayden Panettiere, who was best known for her roles in Heroes and Nashville, has died aged 36. Her death was confirmed by her representatives and followed by a statement.

The statement from her father, Skip, read: “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden. She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen.”

Meanwhile, her mother spoke the first time on Tuesday, firing shots at ex Brian Hickerson. She said: "I think Hayden was an amazingly talented person in so many departments and I think young people who grow up in the entertainment industry -- it is a struggle and it's a very challenging industry and it's not unusual for them to sadly find the wrong path."

She also added: "This person in her life that we have been trying to get rid of for quite some time was with her at her death, and that was Brian Hickerson."

The Coroner's office confirmed that Hayden's autopsy showed 'no signs of trauma' at the time of her death. It had been reported that the police were responding to a call about a suspected "cardiac arrest". A police report later revealed that both her ex Hickerson and his brother Zach were at the scene at the time of her death.

911 audio footage also heard dispatchers discuss a suspected overdose. Both Narcan and Epinephrine were reportedly brought to the scene by emergency services Panettiere's cause of death has not been announced at this time.

A preliminary police investigation has confirmed there were no signs of "foul play or suspicious circumstances" when they arrived at her home after a 911 emergency call from an acquaintance of Panettiere's.

News.title: Influencer mum, 33, falls ill and dies following 'three-in-one' cosmetic surgery
News.content:
Influencer mum, 33, falls ill and dies following 'three-in-one' cosmetic surgery

Instagram influencer and mum-of-three Marta Kelly de Oliveira Silva has tragically died after reports suggest she underwent a combination of three cosmetic procedures

View 3 Images Marta Kelly de Oliveira Silva has sadly died in Brazil (Image: JamPress)

A mum-of-three has died aged just 33 after developing complications following cosmetic surgery.

‌



Marta Kelly de Oliveira Silva underwent surgery on August 12 before being discharged the following day. She was admitted to hospital in Volta Redonda, Brazil on August 14 after becoming unwell, and died in intensive care on Monday.

‌



Reports suggest she underwent a 'three-in-one' combination of procedures including liposuction, breast implants and a tummy tuck, although her family has not confirmed exactly what surgery she had.

‌



Her devastated husband Marcus Vinícius announced her death the following day, writing: “We lost the battle. It is still so difficult to write these words.

“I don’t think any sentence could possibly explain the depth of the pain I am feeling right now. Marta was the love of my life.

View 3 Images She leaves behind a husband and three children (Image: JamPress)

‌



Met Office names 44 areas facing storms and power cuts with 22 hours of warnings READ MORE :

“My best friend, my companion, the best wife I could ever have had and an extraordinary mother to our children. She fought until the very last moment. She fought with all the strength she had.

“And anyone who knew Marta knows exactly who she was: a pure-hearted, shy, simple person, with a way all her own of loving and caring for those around her.”

Originally from Volta Redonda, Marta was mum to three boys. The influencer had amassed 267,000 followers on Instagram, where she shared glimpses of motherhood, family life and her daily routine. The couple had been together for 15 years.

‌



Marta’s family has not revealed where the plastic surgery was carried out or the nature of the complications she developed. She was laid to rest in Volta Redonda on Tuesday morning.

View 3 Images Reports suggest she underwent a 'three-in-one' combination of procedures (Image: JamPress)

Paying tribute to his wife and the mother of his children, Marcus wrote: “As a wife, she was my partner in absolutely everything. As a mother, she was love, care, protection and devotion.

Article continues below

“Théo, Ravi and Filippo had the privilege of having a mother who loved them in a way that words will never be able to explain.

“And now the hardest mission of my life begins: moving forward and raising our three boys in the way she would have wanted.

“I will do everything I can to make sure they grow up knowing exactly who their mother was, how much she loved them and how she will be present in every part of their lives.”

News.title: Common breakfast 'mistake' could be why you're always hungry again by 11am
News.content:
Common breakfast 'mistake' could be why you're always hungry again by 11am

Stay fuller until lunch and avoid reaching for biscuits, crisps or cereal bars by 11am

View 3 Images Always hungry by 11am? Your breakfast could be missing one crucial thing (Image: Getty)

If you’re constantly raiding the biscuit tin before lunch, your breakfast could be to blame. Health specialists say people who seem to be always hungry again by 11am could be missing one crucial thing from their breakfast.

‌



However, a simple 30-second check before your first bite could help keep hunger at bay and leave you feeling fuller for longer, a nutritionist says. Many popular breakfasts are packed with carbohydrates, but fall short on the nutrients that help keep you satisfied throughout the morning.

‌



That means you could be reaching for crisps, chocolate or cereal bars just a couple of hours after eating - even if you’ve had what looks like a decent-sized breakfast. Rather than cutting calories or skipping meals, specialists say making a few simple tweaks to what’s on your plate can make a big difference.

‌



One nutritionist recommends carrying out what he calls a 'Breakfast Check' before you start eating. Oliver Goble, nutritionist at Supply Life, said it takes less than 30 seconds and involves asking yourself three simple questions before your first bite.

He said: "People often think they’re hungry because they haven’t eaten enough, but more often it’s because their breakfast wasn’t balanced in the first place. Taking a few seconds to check what’s on your plate can help you build a meal that’s much more satisfying."

View 3 Images The three-question “breakfast check” could help people stay fuller until lunch (stock image)

‌



The breakfast check

The first question Oliver urges people to ask themselves is: "Where is my protein?" He says protein helps slow digestion and is one of the nutrients most closely linked with helping people feel fuller after eating.

The second question is: "Where’s my fibre?" Oliver explains that foods such as oats, berries, wholegrain bread, fruit, seeds and high-fibre cereals help add bulk to meals and support steadier energy levels throughout the morning.

The final question is: "Will this realistically keep me full until lunch?" Oliver says if your breakfast is mostly sugary or refined carbohydrates, you may find yourself hungry again much sooner than expected.

‌



He said: "You don’t need a perfect breakfast and you certainly don’t need expensive healthy foods. The aim is simply to include a balance of protein, fibre and healthy fats wherever possible, as these nutrients work together to help keep you satisfied."

View 3 Images Protein and fibre can help with lasting satisfaction

Small swaps can make a big difference

Simple changes can make breakfast far more filling without adding lots of extra effort. Oliver says adding Greek yoghurt and berries to cereal, topping porridge with nuts or seeds, choosing wholegrain toast instead of white, or including eggs alongside your breakfast can all help create a meal that’s more balanced.

‌



Oliver added: "When breakfast keeps you satisfied for longer, you’re naturally less likely to spend the rest of the morning thinking about food. It’s a small daily habit, but one that can have a surprisingly big impact over time."

What foods are rich in fibre?

The NHS says: "Most of us need to eat more fibre and have fewer added sugars in our diet. Eating plenty of fibre is associated with a lower risk of heart disease, stroke, type 2 diabetes and bowel cancer."

A higher-fibre breakfast could include cereal such as plain wholewheat biscuits (like Weetabix) or plain shredded whole grain (like Shredded Wheat), or porridge as oats are also a good source of fibre. Go for wholemeal or granary breads, or higher-fibre white bread, and choose wholegrains like wholewheat pasta, bulgur wheat or brown rice.

‌



Go for potatoes with their skins on, such as a baked potato or boiled new potatoes. Add pulses like beans, lentils or chickpeas to stews, curries and salads. Include plenty of vegetables with meals, either as a side dish or added to sauces, stews or curries.

Have some fresh or dried fruit, or fruit canned in natural juice for dessert. Because dried fruit is sticky, it can increase the risk of tooth decay, so it's better if it is only eaten as part of a meal, rather than as a between-meal snack. For snacks, try fresh fruit, vegetable sticks, rye crackers, oatcakes, and unsalted nuts or seeds.

‌



What foods are rich in protein?

Meat, chicken, and fish:

Fresh, unprocessed meat, chicken, and fish are lowest in salt and phosphate

Dairy:

Milk.

Yoghurt – look for higher protein options with more than 7g of protein per 100g such as Skyr or Liberté.

Cheese.

News.title: Much-loved 'Treenis' woodland chopped down despite local outcry
News.content:
A beloved phallic-shaped woodland known as "Penis Woods" is being cut down, despite backlash from the local communities.

Castle Crawford Wood rises up a hillside south of Biggar and caught the eyes of travellers for about 20 years. The trees on Twegill Hill just off the M74 have been "welcoming people to Scotland" for two centuries.

But plans to fell the woodland, known as the "Treenis" due to its distinctive outline, sparked a petition to save it. Locals said the trees should be a "protected landmark".

The petition starter wrote: "The Penis Woodland is a cultural landmark visible from the M74 in Scotland. This iconic cultivation is going to be felled.

Roses will bloom all summer as Alan Titchmarsh hands out vital advice

TikTok’s ‘free day out’ trend is booming — but some could land you in trouble

"It's not just any woodland, it's a penis shaped woodland, visible from the motorway." A spokesman for Scottish Forestry said: "Castle Crawford Wood, which was originally planted in the late 1800s, has reached the end of its natural lifecycle and is experiencing significant windblow, leaving many remaining trees unstable and at risk of further failure.

"Following assessment and public consultation, Scottish Forestry has approved the felling of the woodland, which is in progress. This forms part of the wood’s long-established management, with the site having been felled and replanted several times throughout its history.

"The area is required to be restocked with an appropriate mix of trees species, helping to ensure a sustainable woodland long-term."

News.title: Thunderstorm warnings issued for parts of UK with flash flooding expected
News.content:
Yellow thunderstorm warnings have been issued across the UK, with heavy showers expected to lead to flash flooding and travel disruption.

The Met Office warnings will come into force across northern England, Northern Ireland and eastern Scotland later in the day on Wednesday. The warning for northern England will remain in place until Thursday morning.

The downpours follow almost two months of dry weather, with parts of the country experiencing their first rain in weeks on Tuesday.

People in areas impacted by thunderstorms have been told by the Met Office to expect that businesses and homes could flood, transport services could be delayed and power cuts are likely.

The yellow weather warnings are in place for:

Northern Ireland from 12:00 until 23:59 BST on Wednesday

Parts of North East Scotland, including Aberdeen, from 14:00 until 21:00 on Wednesday

Parts of the North of England, including Manchester and Newcastle upon Tyne, from 19:00 until 10:00 on Thursday

The Met Office said lightning, hail and thunder were expected in the areas affected by warnings, with up to 30mm of rain expected within a few hours in parts of North East Scotland and across Northern Ireland.

Parts of northern England could see up to 50mm of rain within six hours.

Much of the UK has seen a mixture of sunshine and scattered showers already on Wednesday.

In Wisley, Surrey, a 62-day long dry spell was broken on Wednesday morning, with the remarkable run ending after 1.6mm fell before 10.00.

News.title: Israeli army orders criminal investigation into killing of Palestinian girl Hind Rajab in Gaza
News.content:
The Israeli army has ordered a criminal investigation into the killing in Gaza of six-year-old Hind Rajab, whose death was internationally condemned after a desperate recording of her speaking to paramedics was broadcast around the world.

The Palestinian child was one of seven family members travelling in a vehicle that came under Israeli fire in Gaza City in January 2024.

She initially survived the attack that killed several family members, but her body was recovered days later along with her relatives and two paramedics who had tried to save her in an ambulance.

In a statement, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said that "following a review of the findings" and "due to alleged failures in the coordination of the movement of the Palestine Red Crescent ambulance, it has been decided to initiate a criminal investigation of the incident by Military Police Criminal Investigation Division".
