Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 16: Manchester United
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 5th (NB: this is not necessarily Jamie Jackson’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 3rd

Prospects

The information at the start of the close season was that Manchester United planned to trade for bargains rather than elite names and the major purchases so far this summer prove this to indeed be the case. Youri Tielemans is a 29-year-old who has been a professional for nearly half of his life and was bought, with no competition, for his £35m release clause from Aston Villa. The midfielder was followed by the £48m (+£2m) purchase of Andrey Santos, a 22-year-old with 11 league starts last season for Chelsea. The Brazilian states a preference for operating “deep, like a No 6” making him the direct replacement for his compatriot Casemiro, whose CV includes five Champions Leagues. United are also set to sign another midfielder in Carlos Baleba from Brighton for around £75m.

Michael Carrick, going in to his first full season in charge, admits his squad needs more additions and a new left-back is on the radar. Lewis Hall is the prime target but Newcastle’s resistance to a sale means Arsenal’s Myles Lewis-Skelly had drawn interest. At the window’s commencement, Carrick wanted Elliot Anderson but this was unrealistic – he went to City for around £32m more than Tielemans’ and Santos’s combined fee. Confirmed as manager in May after guiding United to third, Carrick may rue Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s reluctance to invest the finances he generated by taking the club back into the Champions League and the 45-year-old may find himself engulfed in precisely what has plagued all of his predecessors in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era: a crisis of performances and results.

Carrick also has to wrestle with the Marcus Rashford situation: the forward wants to leave, the club desires him off the wage bill, but can a suitor be found before 1 September? Oh and, Lisandro Martínez and Matthijs De Ligt, two frontline centre-backs, have only recently returned from injury.

Off-field picture

In early July United unveiled plans for their proposed new 100,000-seater stadium, located about 350 metres north-west of Old Trafford, insisting this is a “sanity, not vanity project”. Behind the catchy line, however, is a club in the red to the sum of £1.3bn. Omar Berrada, United’s chief executive, declared in March that £2bn was the working cost of the stadium, which is projected to be completed in 2035. This seems optimistic – try doubling it, maybe.

Owner-fan relationship

Untrusting, unhappy, annoyed, betrayed, toxic, broken, unmendable, etcetera: choose your pejorative when it comes to describing how most Manchester United fans feel about the Glazers. This has been the case regarding the six siblings, who are United’s majority owners, since Sir Alex Ferguson left the club in May 2013. Relations between fans and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s football department could also be rosier. Some are content due to last season’s third-place finish and the success of last summer’s buys – Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbuemo primarily. Others, though, are cheesed off about the current window’s business, the moving of season-ticket holders around the ground to free up seats for corporate packages, and the recent bid to eliminate touts that caused many genuine supporters to have to prove their innocence.

The manager

Like Ole Gunnar Solskjær before him, Carrick performed superbly in a caretaker capacity. The task now facing him is out-performing his former United team-mate and friend in the role of permanent manager, the Norwegian’s first full season in charge having ended in third place. Carrick’s prospects will be improved if by 1 September a left-back has been recruited. Given Arsenal, Manchester City, Liverpool, Chelsea and Tottenham have splashed far more cash than United on strengthening this summer, Carrick would no doubt take third – or any Champions League berth – if it was offered to him, albeit he is unlikely to admit as much.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Manchester United’s new midfield signing Youri Tielemans in action during a training session in Dublin. Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images

After being a major part of Aston Villa’s Europa League glory in May, and then captaining Belgium to the World Cup quarter-finals during the summer, Tielemans has been recruited to add drive, quality and a streetwisen touch to United’s midfield. His career shows a record of making the difference when required – he struck a memorable volley against Freiburg in Istanbul and powered in a long-range winner to claim the FA Cup for Leicester in 2021. There is no doubt about it – the son of Flemish Brabant is a big-game footballer.

Stat attack

Manchester United led the Premier League for shots last season, with 596. Much will depend upon Bruno Fernandes if they are to repeat this feat. He created at least 89 chances more than any other member of the squad and only fell six shy of taking the most shots. Fernandes turns 32 in early September; can he outrun age for another season?

Set for a breakthrough

Shea Lacey, the quick-footed diminutive winger from Liverpool, made four appearances under three different managers last season. On 21 December, an 84th-minute debut in the 2-1 loss at Aston Villa under Ruben Amorim made him academy product No 256 to feature for United. Eighteen days later, entering again on 84 minutes in the 2-2 draw at Burnley, Lacey’s next cameo was for Darren Fletcher. Fast-forward four days and Lacey lasted only 27 minutes of United’s 2-1 defeat to Brighton in the FA Cup after being sent off late on, later apologising. The 19-year-old had to wait five months before making his next appearance for United, this time under Carrick, entering in the 62nd minute of the final-day 3-0 victory at Brighton. He is now very much part of the first-team squad and one to watch.

World Cup impact

When England needed to stymie Argentina’s second-half onslaught in last month’s World Cup semi-final, with Anthony Gordon having put them 1-0 up, Thomas Tuchel became passive. Off went Gordon and Declan Rice and on came Ezri Konza and Nico O’Reilly. England subsequently crumpled, going on to lose 2-1. If Tuchel had instead turned to Kobbie Mainoo, a ball-carrying midfielder who could retain possession and move England up the field, Argentina may well have been thwarted. As it turned out, Mainoo did not play a second of the tournament. “I was in contact with him quite a bit through the summer [as] I’ve been in that position myself and not played at a World Cup,” Carrick said.

Sports.title: Aston Villa expect another bid from Al Hilal for Ollie Watkins
Sports.content:
Aston Villa are braced for another bid from Al Hilal for Ollie Watkins, after rejecting an offer worth almost £40m for the striker. Al Hilal are pursuing a move for Villa’s all-time Premier League goalscorer, who has reached double figures in the top flight in his six seasons at the club after joining from Brentford.

If Villa sell Watkins, who has two years remaining on his contract, they would seek to replace the 30-year-old England striker and Unai Emery is a big admirer of Nicolas Jackson, but Chelsea’s valuation of £65m is thought to be prohibitive to any deal. There is an acceptance at Villa that any marquee arrival before the close of the window would probably have to follow another major sale, owing to Premier League’s financial regulations.

Emery has had to significantly reshape his squad this summer after the departures of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, who joined Chelsea, Manchester United and Paris Saint-Germain respectively. Rogers left in a deal worth £117m to become the most expensive British player.

Villa have signed Zion Suzuki as a replacement for Emiliano Martínez, whose future remains unclear. Suzuki, a £30m buy from Parma, will be the first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Premier League.

Villa have completed the £17m signing of Matteo Ruggeri from Atlético Madrid and remain in talks with Bayern Munich over a deal for João Palhinha and West Ham for Aaron Wan-Bissaka. Villa have also signed Johan Manzambi from Freiburg for a club-record £52m and Joao Gomes from Wolves for £38m.

There could be further sales, with Villa hoping to find Martínez a new club, while Arsenal remain interested in signing the England defender Ezri Konsa.

Villa gave Watkins, together with Martínez and Konsa, an extended four-week break after the World Cup. Emery said Watkins volunteered to play in last week’s Super Cup, but the manager advised him to continue to rest.

Sports.title: WSL’s ‘big two’: Arsenal and Chelsea record more revenue than rest of league combined | Tom Garry
Sports.content:
After reviewing eight seasons’ worth of Women’s Super League clubs’ financial accounts, it seems appropriate to start by offering a sincere apology to any reader who has become accustomed to seeing the phrase “the big four” in Women’s Super League coverage in reference to Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester City and Manchester United. Financially speaking, that is a myth. There has actually been no such thing in recent times. There has, in fact, been a big two: Arsenal and Chelsea.

On the pitch that quartet have lifted every major domestic women’s trophy since 2014 but, off it, the two London clubs have left the rest of the pack in their dust in regard to wages and turnover, together recording more revenue in 2024-25 than the rest of the division combined.

There are several other striking trends across the data. Namely, rapidly rising revenues and rapidly rising expenditure, as well as a heavy reliance on club owners to fund the sizeable losses. Cumulatively, WSL clubs have recorded post-tax losses of more than £111m when combining all of the figures available since the division switched to a winter calendar in the summer of 2017.

Resisting that pattern are Manchester United, who have recorded a profit of £1.34m since relaunching their senior women’s team in the summer of 2018. In contrast, Chelsea have lost more than £36m over the same timeframe, and there are four further clubs – Brighton and Hove Albion, Leicester City, Manchester City and Tottenham Hotspur – who have each lost eight-figure sums when adding up their losses across those years.

United, who this summer have made clear their intention to focus on youth development in an attempt to build long-term success, believing current levels of spending in the transfer market are unsustainable, are a unique case study. In the 2022-23 campaign, when they finished second, missing out on the WSL title on the season’s final day, their wages amounted to under 50% of their revenue, in a season when Manchester City, Tottenham and Brighton all spent more than 100% of their revenue on wages. This is not uncommon across men’s and women’s football. A recent report from Deloitte, for example, highlighted that 13 men’s Championship clubs spent more on wages than their revenue in 2024-25, with that division’s collective wage bill growing to more than £900m and to 96% of revenue.

Wages for elite women’s players are soaring – – on average across the WSL they quadrupled between 2019 and 2025. Revenues rose strongly over that timeframe too, with the largest chunk of matchday revenue growth coming at Arsenal, whose gate receipts were just £45,000 per season nine years ago and totalled nearly £6m in 2024-25. On average across WSL clubs, for whom data is available, wages rose by 28.2% between 2023-24 and 2024-25, while over the same period post-tax losses increased by more than 53%, albeit a large chunk of that can be apportioned to Chelsea’s purchase of their former home ground, Kingsmeadow, from their parent club for about £12m during 2024-25.

Chelsea – who won the league for a sixth straight year in 2024-25 – had a total wage bill that was more than five times larger than an Everton side who finished eighth in the WSL, and just under three times that of Manchester United, who finished third that season. Arsenal were the only other club, along with Chelsea, whose wage bill exceeded £10m. Both clubs recorded turnover that was around twice that of their Manchester rivals. Significantly, that came before their respective spending in the summer 2025 window, when Arsenal broke the £1m barrier to land the Canada winger Olivia Smith and Chelsea followed suit later that summer with the signing of Alyssa Thompson.

Overall, the WSL has had a 75% increase in agents’ fees year-on-year, according to data released by the Football Association, with Chelsea exceeding the £1m mark last season. In comparison, West Ham, who finished 10th in 2025-26, spent £97,000, while relegated Leicester spent less than a tenth of what Chelsea did.

Soon then there could be a new force in the WSL in the shape of London City Lionesses. Their wage bill for 2024-25, when they won promotion from the second tier, has not been made public, but their operating loss of £10.6m was more than 10 times their revenue of £902,000. That came before dramatic moves in the transfer market across the past three windows, which have included the signing of former Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas.

As the WSL now gears up for the 2026-27 campaign – the first in which there are expected to be points penalties on the line for any teams whose player wage bills exceed a threshold of “80% of your revenue plus up to £4m of owners’ contributions” – the season ahead is one where the financial accounts will matter more than ever.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 15: Manchester City
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 2nd (NB: this is not necessarily Jamie Jackson’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 2nd

Prospects

Enzo Maresca was already in herculean task mode by signing on as the man charged with continuing the dynasty built by Pep Guardiola at Manchester City before Rodri decided to leave the club and join Barcelona. The 30-year-old may be headed for a second Ballon d’Or after his displays in Spain’s triumphant World Cup campaign, so the loss of a midfielder capable of moulding games domestically and in the Champions League represents a sizeable blow for Maresca.

There are further negatives too, with John Stones, Nathan Aké and Bernardo Silva also no longer at City. On the positive side, Elliot Anderson has joined for £116m from Nottingham Forest having impressed for England at the World Cup. City’s new manager also has Erling Haaland, who will be favourite to claim a fourth Premier League Golden Boot in five seasons. Less certain is how Phil Foden will perform despite being boosted by a bumper new contract. Can the boy from Stockport dovetail with Rayan Cherki and once more pull the strings for his boyhood side?

Off-field picture

City are a best-in-class organisation, who can be used as an exemplar of how to pursue excellence on and off the field. This, of course, would change were they found guilty over the 130 charges brought against them for alleged breaches of Premier League rules. It has been more than three years since the charges were announced, with City continuing to deny any wrongdoing. The new Pep Guardiola Stand, opened for the great man’s final home game last season, means 61,000 fans can now witness Haaland and co go to work, the Etihad Stadium’s capacity having previously stood at 53,400.

Owner-fan relationship

Sheikh Mansour is a hero to the City faithful for a glittering period of ownership that has elevated their team to a domestic and continental superpower. Listening to fans, the club have also frozen ticket prices for a third consecutive season. Meanwhile in the Pep Guardiola Stand, 4,000 new flexi season tickets – a pay-as-you-go scheme – have sold out, half of which are for junior fans, with City introducing £10 seats for those who live in the five wards around the ground.

The manager

Is Maresca courageous for following The Man or naive for believing he can? Over to the 46-year-old, who has zero doubt the City job is no chalice laced with poison. “It’s fantastic, nice and exciting, and for me, a privilege,” he said. “First of all, the most important thing has been that Khaldoon [al-Mubarak, the chair], Hugo [Viana, the director of football] and Ferran [Soriano, the chief executive] all speak the same language in terms of this is a club that has to win games, titles and has to compete, but we also talk about how we can continue to make this club better, season after season.” Maresca’s CV shows the Championship crown with Leicester, and the Conference League and Club World Cup glory with Chelsea. How he would love to add the Premier League title to that roll of honour at the first time of asking.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Elliot Anderson of Manchester City holds off Martin Ødegaard and Myles Lewis-Skelly of Arsenal during the 2026 FA Community Shield. Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images

Rodri’s departure offers Anderson an opportunity to run City’s midfield. Can he do so? Maresca and Viana obviously believe this or £116m would not have been splurged on the lad from Whitley Bay who could not nail down a starting berth for Newcastle in five years as a senior professional there. At the World Cup there were flashes of a schemer who can spray passes long range – Rodri-style – as well as the shorter, metronomic stuff. What’s for sure is that Anderson has a career-defining opportunity in front of him.

Stat attack

Manchester City conceded more league goals from set pieces last season than they had in the previous two campaigns combined. They were costly at times too: the winning goals in their losses at Aston Villa and Newcastle both came from corners, for instance. Maresca’s Chelsea conceded from a set play every three league games so his record there was a shade worse than City’s in 2025-26. He has work to do.

Set for a breakthrough

Vitor Reis was signed in January 2025 and made four appearances that season. The defender’s debut was also forgettable as, then 19, he was hooked at half-time with City trailing 1-0 at Leyton Orient in the FA Cup fourth round. The Brazilian played all of the 3-1 victory in the following round, and was fielded in the 89th-minute of the 2-0 league victory at Leicester in April before his sole other City appearance: a full outing in the 2-0 Club World Cup win over Wydad Casablanca that June. Last season’s loan at City’s sister club Girona ended in relegation, but Reis is said to have impressed.

World Cup impact

The departed Rodri made real the ultimate fantasy of all players by captaining his country to the World Cup and being so vital to that glory that he was named player of the tournament. Cherki fared less well, making six substitute appearances and one start for a France side that fell, to Spain, in the semi-finals. France’s attacking ranks may overflow with quality, but for a player with magic in both boots, that seemed odd.

Sports.title: Is Turkey home to savvy signings or a new retirement league? We’ll soon find out
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah plays in Turkey now. So do Romelu Lukaku and Leandro Trossard and Leroy Sané and Nathan Aké. Mason Greenwood and N’Golo Kanté and Dusan Vlahovic, too.

Bruno Fernandes and Gabriel Martinelli may yet follow them there, depending on negotiations and moods and whatever else compels a footballer to leave one club for another.

Victor Osimhen, one of the world’s highest-rated strikers, was already at Galatasaray, where he has hammered in 43 league goals in two seasons, plus this campaign’s opener.

Salah, the Super Lig’s signature signing, will reportedly earn about as much at Trabzonspor as he did with Liverpool last season, where he was one of the Premier League’s highest earners – on account of the net salary structure in Turkey.

As the Saudi Pro League, which flooded the game with billions in cash when it lured Cristiano Ronaldo and Neymar in 2023, scales back its ambitions, the Turkish league has stepped into the void. A flurry of investment by its four biggest clubs – Galatasaray, Fenerbahce, Besiktas and Trabzonspor – is remaking it into the new moneyed destination league for the game’s ageing and the underplayed and the overpaid and the overvalued. Or perhaps they’ve made a series of savvy signings; we’ll soon find out.

Unlike in previous spending sprees by leagues seeking to claim a more prominent spot in the transfer market ecosystem, the Super Lig doesn’t seem to have benefited from massive investment from a soft-power nation-building project or the sudden interest of oligarchs. Rather – and it’s all slightly confounding – it appears to have more to do with the collapse of the Turkish lira relative to the euro, which went from trading at €0.10 half a decade ago to about €0.018 today. While their clubs pay their players in lira, revenue from European competition and foreign broadcasts is paid out in euros. The long and short of it is that the big four Turkish clubs can now afford players they previously couldn’t because they can write down more of their earnings on their balance sheets.

As such, Turkey joins an increasingly long line of unconventional homes for some of the game’s biggest names. Every few years, some new league invests heavily in hopes of finding a shortcut into the firmament of the world’s best-regarded competitions. Before Saudi Arabia, it was China, where it was the stated objective of President Xi Jinping and his government to leverage the sport as “a must to build China into a sports powerhouse as part of the Chinese dream”. Eventually, Chinese soccer awoke from that dream with a start.

Before that, it was the Russian Premier League, when sanctioned oil billionaire Suleyman Kerimov bought Anzhi Makhachkala and plowed in hundreds of millions to lure some of the world’s top players. That set off an arms race with Zenit St Petersburg, Rubin Kazan and Dynamo Moscow, before the spending fever broke just a few years later when Kerimov backed off.

The Brazilian league has had flurries of pricey signings over the years – although mostly focused on bringing home the country’s wayward sons – in apparent accordance with the state of the nation’s economy and bank balances. In January, Flamengo brought Lucas Paquetá back from West Ham for an astounding $50m, setting a new Brazilian record for an incoming transfer, dwarfing the $32m Cruzeiro had paid Zenit for Gerson just 20 days earlier.

During its Beckham Era, Major League Soccer was routinely paying above-market rates to lure Thierry Henry, Robbie Keane and the like. And before that, the Qatar Stars League tried to deliver on its name by drawing Gabriel Batistuta, Pep Guardiola, Frank de Boer, Marcel Desailly and others for a final payday.

Every one of these leagues moved on from this gambit before long, switching to some other strategy, or however they spun the decision to cap the money gusher.

It should probably be pointed out here that unlike most of the aforementioned circuits, Turkey actually has a thriving and long-established football and fan culture. That makes it feel slightly different this time around, as Turkish clubs have earned credibility as the homes of star players, unexpected though their arrivals may be, and because those players will probably still appear in the Champions League (Galatasaray qualified automatically; Fenerbahce are in the qualifiers) and Europa League (Trabzonspor and Besiktas are both in the qualifying rounds).

All the same, the Turkish clubs now take the mantle of acting as a kind of bailout fund for Europe’s storied leagues, where clubs from the latter can offload their distressed assets. At a minimum, these nouveaux riche leagues provide a hefty cash injection to the old-money center of the European game.

In the end, nothing much ever comes of this play for the newly ambitious. They move on, eventually. The whole thing turns out to be counterproductive. Because rather than match the status of the legacy competitions they hope to challenge, they wind up bankrolling them, cementing the chasm between them.

They learn that lesson before long and the money dries up. But no matter, there is always some fresh source of dumb money out there.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Al-Hilal eye moves for Harry Kane and Ollie Watkins?
Sports.content:
It seems the possibility of winning the Ballon d’Or is not the only thing the England captain Harry Kane has been talking about recently. Well, his representatives at least. It is thought the Bayern Munich striker’s team have been in talks with the Saudi Pro League’s Al-Hilal with Kane reportedly open to a future move.

However, it’s also understood the 33-year-old wants to remain at the German club with discussions beginning on his new contract in Munich. The Bundesliga transfer window closes on 31 August so if a move east were to happen it would have to be done quickly.

Al-Hilal are not in the market for only one England star though, they are bidding for two. Ollie Watkins is reported to have agreed personal terms with the club, though the Saudi club have not yet officially logged a transfer bid with the 30-year-old’s current club, Aston Villa. Reports differ as to whether Al-Hilal want to bring in only one striker or more, with some claiming the club have turned to Watkins after a deal with Kane did not come to fruition. But who knows? Maybe Watkins and Kane will fight for the starting shirt.

One player who won’t be starting for Manchester United in the upcoming season is Gavi who has turned down the chance to join the Premier League club. The Spain World Cup winner wants to remain at Barcelona.

United fans may be growing frustrated with the lack of star signings this window but concerns are not just about insufficient numbers of players coming through the doors; the Reds are also being raided. Napoli are said to be interested in the forward Joshua Zirkzee. The Netherlands player was largely competing from the bench last season for Michael Carrick’s side.

Napoli seem to have their fingers in any number of pies as they have also reached out to Chelsea about Nicolas Jackson as well as enquiring about Gabriel Jesus at Arsenal. If they were to sign Jesus though they would have to sell one of the forwards in their squad before welcoming the Brazilian star.

Staying in Serie A, Milan have rejected a bid from Coventry for Ruben Loftus-Cheek. The newly promoted Premier League club wanted to bring the 30-year-old midfielder back to the top flight for the first time since 2023 when he played for Chelsea but an £8.5m offer was turned down by the Italian side.

Circling back to the Premier League, Manchester City have lost one of their key players in Rodri, who signed for Barcelona on Tuesday, which has left Enzo Maresca scouring his transfer options in midfield. Among the names on the new manager’s list is Crystal Palace’s Adam Wharton. The price tag for the England international is unclear, which could affect the move given City have already spent £116m on Elliot Anderson in this window.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Finally, Jack Grealish may have been spotted at Cardiff’s 1-1 draw against Wrexham in the Championship on Monday, which sparked rumours of a move to Wales for the 30-year-old but it seems more likely that the England international will remain in the Premier League. That assumption comes after news that Everton’s chief executive, Angus Kinnear, has interest in bringing the star back to Hill Dickinson Stadium after a loan deal last season. But Grealish could also remain at his current club, Manchester City.

Sports.title: ‘This isn’t normal in football’: Xisco, Malaysia and the new Invincibles
Sports.content:
Many Watford fans felt Xisco Muñoz was dismissed too soon after leading them into the Premier League as Championship runners-up in 2021, only to be ousted less than two months into the new season. He is remembered fondly at Vicarage Road, an emblem of the churn-and-burn of the Gino Pozzo era.

But unless you continued to follow the Spaniard’s career closely, you would struggle to guess where he manages now. The life of a football manager is varied and unpredictable, but how has the former Watford head coach ended up in charge of a club 6,500 miles away and on the verge of an extraordinary world record?

Not one averse to adventure – since moving into coaching Xisco has taken jobs in Georgia, Cyprus and Slovakia – the former Valencia and Betis midfielder agreed last summer to take over at the Malaysian Super League side Johor Darul Ta’zim, based just across the border from Singapore.

A remarkable amount of pressure rests on their opening game of the Malaysian Super League season against Kuching on Friday. Avoid defeat and they will set the world record for unbeaten league matches, 109, surpassing the benchmark set by the Ivorian side Asec Mimosas that has stood for 32 years.

Xisco likes the idea that, in a football world dominated by the financial clout of European clubs, this is a record none of the household names are ever likely to surpass.

But he stresses that while JDT are backed by the resources of the Malaysian royal family – ever since His Royal Highness Major General Tunku Ismail ibni Sultan Ibrahim, known more aptly as the Crown Prince, bought the club in 2013 and turned them into a sort of Manchester City of Malaysia – it is by no means easy.

“It’s difficult to not lose one game,” Xisco says from his office in their 40,000-seater Sultan Ibrahim Stadium. “Something might happen – one day someone is sleeping, or after 10 minutes the whole team is sleeping, or maybe you don’t 100% concentrate in the first minutes and you concede two goals and it’s difficult to change the game.”

He credits “the work of the boss in the last 13 years” for putting them in this position. Their 108-game unbeaten streak started in April 2021. “Now it’s only one game. The line is very close between success or frustration. This is important. We are so close to making history for unbeaten games in a row. This isn’t normal in football.”

View image in fullscreen Xisco says he benefits from Premier League-standard facilities at JDT. Photograph: Ashok Kumar/Getty Images

When Xisco was first approached by the Crown Prince, he was sold on “the project” – not only winning trophies in Malaysia but raising the standards of the country’s football and its standing on the global stage. There has been a deliberate effort to follow the European model. JDT’s chief executive is Luis García, the former Champions League winner with Liverpool. The academy director, Javier Ribera, arrived from Valencia. Xisco says JDT’s facilities are comparable to those in the Premier League.

In Europe finances have created a rigidity that is hard to break, with the best players ending up at a handful of clubs. By contrast Xisco believes Asian football is filled with growth potential. He points to the dominance of Real Madrid and Barcelona in Spain, Paris Saint- Germain in France, a clutch of clubs in England. “Every day it’s more difficult to find good players. It’s totally different here. Asia is a place for the future. Europe has problems with their economies. They are in one place and it’s difficult to progress.”

Xisco finds it refreshing to work for an owner who demands the highest standards and supports them financially. If he or his staff need something – a new piece of gym or medical equipment, anything they believe could raise their level – the Crown Prince provides it. “Sometimes you are in some jobs, every time trying to cut some things because you have problems. Here, no. Always try to give the best to reach a high level,” Xisco says.

The Crown Prince is relentlessly ambitious, signs off on everything and even attends many training sessions, arriving with scores of security staff, either in supercars or lengthy motorcades.

“I like everything about him. It’s true. I don’t know how long I will be here. I never know, because football is about results. But right now I’m happy. I feel well with him. He’s a positive voice. He pushes us. He helps me a lot.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

JDT have completed Malaysian football – winning 12 consecutive titles – but the next frontier is the Asian Champions League. Last season, they reached the quarter-finals, the furthest so far by a Malaysian club, losing to the Saudi giants Al-Ahli, whose team included Ivan Toney and Riyad Mahrez. The competition represents another significant cultural shift from Europe. To play the Japanese J1 League side Machida Zelvia away is a 6,000-mile round trip.

“In England, you have one hour 30 minutes by plane to get back. Here maybe you need 10 hours or 12 hours if you go to Japan in the Champions League. You need to manage a lot of situations that are totally different. The culture is totally different between Europe and Asia.”

View image in fullscreen Chelsea’s Liam Delap is tackled by Dejan Petrovic of JDT during a pre-season friendly. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Their domestic dominance can also become a hindrance when a team so used to attacking is forced to defend and players struggle to adapt to new tactical requirements. To counter this, Xisco organises competitive XI v XI training matches, utilising JDT’s vast 40-player squad – a necessity given how many competitions they play – to work on deficiencies.

It helps having Arif Aiman – a 24-year-old known in these parts as the “Asian Messi” who scored in the recent friendly against Chelsea, which ended 3-3. He reminds Xisco of João Pedro, whom he coached at Watford.

Xisco loves his unpredictability and invention, how you can’t take your eyes off him because you might miss him completely change the game. “In modern football, sometimes we don’t have this type of class.”

He adds: “He was one of my big surprises. Sometimes you have a young player, like João Pedro at Watford, in 10 minutes you say, wow, this player is different. Arif is the same. Arif has the same capacity – the capacity to change the game.”

Sports.title: March, May and more: footballers scoring in months that match their names | The Knowledge
Sports.content:
“Birmingham’s August Priske scored the only goal at Swansea in the League Cup on 8 August. Can you think of any other examples of players scoring in their namesake months?” wonders Paul Tiffen.

Our wonderful readers have managed to cover the entire year, pretty much, so let’s get going. The list below includes just some of the many examples you sent in.

January

“Not all last names exist for English months, so I also took month names in some other languages,” writes Mykola Kozlenko. “I only accepted exact spellings, [so] I don’t accept Auguste or Augustin for the month of August, but Agosto is fine.” As is Janvier, which gave Mykola their first goalscorer: “Nicolas Janvier. Scored on 30 January 2016 for Lannion v Rennes Reserves.”

February

“Jayden Fevrier. Scored on 3 February 2024 for Colchester against Forest Green Rovers,” writes Mykola.

March

“In German, March is ‘März’,” writes Dirk Maas. “In the 1992-93 edition of the 2. Bundesliga, Heiko März scored twice in March, for Hansa Rostock against St. Pauli and Darmstadt.” Dirk also points out that Solly March’s portfolio of goals in March includes two for Brighton in FA Cup quarter-finals: against Millwall in 2019 and Grimsby in 2023.

View image in fullscreen Solly March heads home for Brighton in their 5-0 FA Cup quarter-final victory over Grimsby in March 2023. Photograph: Andrew Matthews/PA

April

“April Heinrichs scored twice for the USA on April Fools’ Day 1991 against Yugoslavia in the Grand Hotel Varna Tournament in Bulgaria,” writes Dan Almond. “She also scored on 3 April against Hungary and again in the final as the USA beat USSR 5-0.”

May

“David May scored the opening goal in Manchester United’s final game of the 1995-96 season,” writes Sinan Eccles. “The 3-0 win against Middlesbrough at the Riverside on 5 May 1996 secured the title for United. Andy Cole and Ryan Giggs scored the others. Eric Cantona got the late winner in a 1-0 victory over Liverpool in the FA Cup final to secure United their second domestic double in three seasons.”

View image in fullscreen David May (right) is congratulated by Roy Keane after opening the scoring against Middlesbrough in May 1996. Photograph: Michael Mayhew/Allstar

Matt Beaumont points out that Alfie May scored on 7 May 2023 for Cheltenham Town v Charlton – and then joined the Addicks two months later, leaving as Cheltenham’s record goalscorer.

June

Back to Mykola Kozlenko: “Brazil’s Edigar Junio scored on 22 June 2019 for Yokohama F Marinos against Matsumoto Yamaga in the J-League.”

View image in fullscreen Edigar Junio scores the winner for Yokohama F Marinos in their J-League match against Matsumoto Yamaga in June 2019. Photograph: Masashi Hara/Getty Images

July

Three goalscoring Julios in July were found by Mykola …

Anderson Julio (Ecuador), 13 July 2023, Real Salt Lake v Sporting KC

Jhojan Julio (Ecuador), 31 July 2019, LDU Quito v Olimpia

Junior Julio Bueno (Armenia), 20 July 2023, Ararat-Armenia v Egnatia

View image in fullscreen Anderson Julio wheels away in celebration after scoring for Real Salt Lake at Sporting Kansas City in July 2023. Photograph: Bill Barrett/ISI Photos/Getty Images

August

Michael St John-Mcalister offers August Lohapresert, the Sweden-born midfielder who won an under-23 cap for Thailand. Turns out the internet isn’t entirely bad, for it has provided details of Gais Under-19’s 2-1 victory over Kalmar FF Under-19s on 16 August 2012. Both Gais’s goals were scored by their substitute, the aforementioned Lohapresert.

September

Back to Mykola for the last few. “Mateusz Wrzesien (Poland). Scored on 26 September 2018 for Baltyk Koszalin v Rozwoj Katowice.” We should probably clarify that Wrzesien is September in Polish.

October

Pasquale Ottobre scored a brace on 25 October 2009 for Fidelis Andros against Virtus Lanciano in Italy’s Lega Pro. (Note: Pasquale is a name usually given to those born around Easter or Passover, although Ottobre was born in … November.)

November

Tymofiy Lystopad (Ukraine). Scored on 7 November 2015 in Desna Chernihiv v Naftovyk-Ukrnafta Okhtyrka. Lystopad is November in Ukrainian

December

This was the only month for which we didn’t receive a goalscoring answer, but Mykola Kozlenko did find a manager: Frantz Décembre, the Haitian who managed several clubs in the 2010s. We don’t have a specific game, but it’s probably a fair bet that at least one of his teams scored at least one goal in December.

Caught in no-man’s land

“In the recent Leagues Cup clash between Tigres and Vancouver Whitecaps, Tigres goalkeeper Nahuel Guzmán received a straight red card for pushing the referee. The incident took place near the halfway line. What is the furthest upfield that a goalkeeper has received a straight red card?” asks Eoin Fegan.

Back in 2015, West Ham’s Adrián came forward for a corner late on against Leicester at Upton Park – but when the ball was cleared and the visitors threatened to break, the keeper caught Jamie Vardy with a high boot, and was shown a straight red card. Adrián insisted that the foul was accidental, tweeting: “Never in my career I have kicked nobody with bad intention to deserve a red card.” West Ham appealed the decision, but it was upheld and Adrián received a three-match ban.

Knowledge archive

In the Highland League match on 8 August between Forres Mechanics and Fraserburgh, Forres defender Ewan Neil was sent off for a foul just seven seconds after the match kicked off, and Fraserburgh awarded a penalty kick,” writes Sid Bright. “What is the quickest penalty ever awarded in a match?”

We previously looked at this topic in 2017, after a similar question from Stephen Yoxall. He saw his team, Witton Albion, win a penalty after six seconds in an FA Trophy tie against Chester FC when Tolani Omotola was fouled by Blaine Hudson.

Here’s what we wrote at the time: “Witton’s penalty was awarded after just 6.18 seconds. It was saved, but Bradley Bauress followed up his own spot-kick to score the rebound. Omotola was then sent off later in the first half, before Hudson – probably fortunate to avoid a dismissal with the initial penalty – picked up a second booking during the second period. Witton’s coach Paul Moore was later sent to the stands, before the visitors’ Matthew Devine gave away a late penalty, which earned him a red card, and Chester an equaliser. The nine men were beaten when Chester’s Elliott Durrell grabbed an injury-time winner.”

We found a number of other early examples, but nothing to beat 6.18 seconds – we even had a word with the people behind the Guinness Book of World Records. Forres Mechanics went close with their recent effort, but we have found a quicker penalty, awarded to Tanzania in a World Cup qualifier against Madagascar in September 2021.

As reported by the BBC, Tanzania launched it long from kick off, and Simon Msuva was brought down on the edge of the area by Madagascar keeper Melvin Adrien. The foul was committed after just four seconds, with the spot-kick given a second later. Erasto Nyoni stepped up to convert it, setting the hosts up for a 3-2 victory.

Are there any faster penalties we’ve missed? Get in touch …

Can you help?

“Marquinhos won his 40th trophy in club football when Paris Saint-Germain beat Aston Villa in the Super Cup,” notes Paul Gage. “Has any player won more?”

View image in fullscreen Another one for the collection: Marquinhos with the Uefa Super Cup. Photograph: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images

“The last full-time England manager to have won the English top flight as a coach was Don Revie (1974-77). Does any country have a longer drought?” asks Albert from Vienna.

“Midnite are the 26-27 shirt sponsors for three Championship sides; Middlesbrough, Sheffield United and Wolves,” notes Peter Skilton. “This means they will be the sponsors of at least one of the teams in 24% of Championship fixtures this season. “Is this a record, and which brand has sponsored the most different teams in a single league?”

“On 11 July 2010, Maarten Stekelenburg and Gregory van der Wiel played in the World Cup final against Spain,” begins Dirk Maas. “Seventeen days later came their next match, for Ajax against PAOK in the Champions League qualifiers. Have any other European players played their next competitive game so soon after a World Cup final?

“Arsenal Tivat have truly embodied the boring, boring Arsenal stereotype by starting the Montenegrin league season with three successive 0-0 draws. Has any side ever managed to start a season in a less entertaining manner than this?” asks Richard Wilson.

“When watching the new Mourinho documentary on Netflix, there was some footage of old Portuguese football – I think it was Vitória Setubal or Belenenses – and the goalmouth had a weird sand triangle within the six-yard box. The triangle started at each post and ended in the middle of the six-yard box. It looked like a baseball field. I’ve never seen this before. Was it commonplace in Portugal or anywhere else?” asks Chris Ward.

“Xavi Simons was named after Xavi Hernández, who will be his coach at international level after taking the Netherlands job,” notes Niall McVeigh. “Are there any other examples of footballers playing for coaches they are named after (but not related to)?”

“Has a club’s player-manager ever been called up for an international cap, or travelled to play during an international break in the club season?” asks Frederick Sondheimer-Acosta.

Sports.title: Where to watch Newcastle v Liverpool amid good omen for Andoni Iraola’s first game
Sports.content:
Where to watch Newcastle v Liverpool amid good omen for Andoni Iraola’s first game

Liverpool kick-off their Premier League campaign with a trip to St James' Park, as Alexander Isak returns to Newcastle for the first time.

Sunday marks the dawn of a new era for both clubs, with Andoni Iraola and Matthias Jaissle taking charge of their sides for the first time in the top-flight.



3 St James' Park will see a new manager in the dugout for the first time since 2021 Credit: Getty

The Geordies will undoubtedly make their feelings known towards Liverpool frontman Isak, who missed both meeting between the two teams last season following his £125million switch.

The Sweden international netted just three league goals last term for the Reds and will be eager to reignite his career at his former home.

Former Bournemouth boss Iraola has overseen a major rebuilding project at Liverpool following the departures of several senior figures earlier this summer, including Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson, and Ibrahima Konate.



Meanwhile, the Magpies have sold three of their biggest superstars in Anthony Gordon, Bruno Guimaraes, and Sandro Tonali for an accumulated profit of £240m.

However, the club hierarchy have reinvested those funds into six new recruits and have focused heavily on youth.



Heading into the fixture, history favours the visitors with Liverpool unbeaten in their last 19 Premier League clashes against the Toon, winning 14 and drawing five.

Additionally, Iraola did not lose any of his six Premier League encounters with Newcastle during his tenure in charge of Bournemouth.



Where to watch Newcastle v Liverpool

This fixture will be played on Sunday, August 23 and is scheduled to kick-off at 4:30pm.

The match will be broadcast live on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Premier League following the conclusion of Manchester City v AFC Bournemouth.

3 Ngumoha may become the Premier League's shining starlet after there was more calls to Arne Slot last season to give the forward more game time Credit: Getty

talkSPORT will have updates from the match on GameDay Live with Sam Matterface, Micky Gray and Perry Groves.



Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app.

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 



talkSPORT.com will also have all the action in our dedicated Premier League blog.

3 Wirtz has shown promising signs in pre-season for Liverpool Credit: AFP

Newcastle v Liverpool: Team news

Isak will be acting as the lone striker as Hugo Ekitike continues his recovery after rupturing his achilles.

Operating behind him will almost certainly be Florian Wirtz, who enjoyed a stellar pre-season campaign.



On the right wing, youngster Rio Ngumoha is expected to feature, competing for a spot alongside new recruit Víctor Munoz.

On the left, Cody Gakpo is expected to start, despite being linked with a move away from the club to Tottenham this summer.

The summer signing Jeremy Jacquet is a doubt in defence for the opener after not playing since February due to injury, though the Frenchman scored on debut in pre-season against Como.

That means Ronald Araujo could come straight into the starting XI, having just signed on loan from Barcelona, with both Joe Gomez and Giovanni Leoni still sidelined.



Meanwhile, Newcastle midfielder Joelinton is out for several weeks with an undisclosed issue, while defenders Tino Livramento and Fabian Schar are both doubtful for their Premier League opening fixture.

Following high-profile departures during the transfer window, Jaissle remains stripped of several key figures from Eddie Howe's successful tenure.

Additionally, while Lewis Miley featured in a recent friendly against Bayer Leverkusen, the midfielder is not expected to be match-ready to start against the Reds.

Sports.title: When is transfer deadline day? Premier League summer window info amid £2billion spending spree
Sports.content:
Deadline day for the 2026 summer transfer window is fast-approaching, with big-money business being completed left, right and centre.

Top-flight clubs have already spent well over £2billion this summer, with still plenty of time to splash more cash.



2 Santos to Man United has been one of the biggest deals of the summer Credit: Getty

There have been multiple record-breaking £100million-plus transfers made in the Premier League despite it being a World Cup summer.

Elliot Anderson has joined Manchester City, Sandro Tonali has signed for Tottenham and Morgan Rogers is now a Chelsea player.

However, time will feel like it's quickly running out for all clubs to get their deals done as the deadline gets closer...



When does the transfer window shut?

The transfer deadline in England is set for Tuesday, September 1.

For the last two windows, the closing time was set for 7pm, but the time will now return to its original later deadline.

It means the summer window closes at 11pm on September 1.

Clubs can submit deal sheets before the deadline to give themselves a two-hour grace period to complete transfers.



This deadline is in place for the Premier League and EFL.

In the WSL, the window closes at 11pm on Thursday, September 3.

And that's the same day as the Scottish Premiership, but in Scotland, the deadline is going to be set for 5pm rather than 11pm.

2 England star Anderson has joined Man City for a record-breaking fee Credit: Getty



When is the deadline across Europe?

For LaLiga clubs, their summer window shuts at a similar time to in England, with the deadline set for September 1 at 10:59pm.

In Italy and Serie A, clubs have until 8pm on the same day.

As for the Bundesliga, their deadline is Monday, August 31 at 7pm.

When does the winter transfer window open?

Once the summer deadline shuts, clubs will not be able to do any more business until the winter window opens.

In England, transfers will be possible again from January 1, 2027.

The window will run for a month, closing again on February 1 at 11pm.

Meanwhile, in the WSL, the winter window will open on January 4 and close exactly a month later on February 4.

And in Scotland, their window will open on January 5, closing at 5pm on February 4.

Sports.title: Arsenal on the verge of signing Ezri Konsa to leave Aston Villa at risk of mass exodus
Sports.content:
Arsenal on the verge of signing Ezri Konsa to leave Aston Villa at risk of mass exodus

Arsenal are on the brink of signing Aston Villa centre-back Ezri Konsa, talkSPORT understands.

The Gunners have made Konsa one of their top targets this summer with star defender William Saliba set for a prolonged period on the sidelines and Jurrien Timber dealing with a groin injury.

3 Saliba's back injury has forced Arsenal into the transfer market this summer Credit: Getty

Villa had already rejected a verbal offer from Arsenal, which was understood to be in the region of £35million, a figure that fell well short of the West Midlands outfit's valuation of £65m.

But the reigning Premier League champions have since ramped up their pursuit just days away from the start of the new season and they are now close to a deal, with personal terms agreed.

Which defenders have been on Arsenal's shortlist this summer?

Arsenal had already drawn up a number of contingency plans had their pursuit of Konsa proved unsuccessful.

The Gunners held discussions with Bayer Leverkusen's Jarell Quansah, although the Bundesliga outfit are reluctant to sell.

Quansah only joined Leverkusen last summer from Liverpool for £35m.

Como's Jacobo Ramon was another defender of interest to Arsenal.

However, any sale of Ramon would net his former employers Real Madrid a healthy boost as they retain a 50 per cent sell-on clause.

Danny Murphy's verdict on Ezri Konsa to Arsenal

But it now appears the Gunners will not need to pursue alternative options, with Konsa's seven-year stay at Villa Park nearing its end.

Reacting to the news on talkSPORT's White and Jordan, former England international Danny Murphy hailed Konsa as a 'super player' and 'great addition' for the Gunners but question how he will fit in when Saliba returns to fitness.

"He's a fantastic player, he's been great for Villa, so I understand the admiration from Arsenal," Murphy said.

3 Konsa joined Villa in 2019 from Brentford and has made 286 appearances for the club Credit: Getty

"It's a step up in terms of trying to win trophies, but when everyone's fit, I don't think he plays ahead of Saliba or Gabriel.

"Most players trust themselves to get into a team and I'm sure he believes in himself, but the reality is, when Saliba gets back and the partnership he has with Gabriel, he's going to be playing in the lesser games.

"Arsenal's strength in depth is very impressive, but Konsa will be a great addition, he's a super player.

"If they get him, they've got a really accomplished and confident player…I'm surprised Villa are letting it happen.

"It leaves a gaping hole for Villa."

Which players have left Aston Villa this summer?

Konsa's mooted exit will add to what has already been a hectic summer of outgoings for the Villans.

3 Emery could lose a significant portion of Villa's spine in one window Credit: Getty

Unai Emery's side has already lost Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers and Lucas Digne.

Rogers moved to Chelsea for an eye-watering £117m, making him the most expensive British player of all-time.

Tielemans joined Manchester United after they triggered his £35m release clause while Digne returned to Paris Saint-Germain for less than £10m.

The high-profile departures from Villa Park may not end with Konsa, as the club rejected a £45m offer from Al-Hilal for striker Ollie Watkins.

There's also uncertainty surrounding Emi Martinez's future following the £30m arrival of Japan international Zion Suzuki from Parma.

Sports.title: Darwin Nunez and Karim Benzema in line for moves as Al Hilal pursue Ollie Watkins
Sports.content:
Darwin Nunez and Karim Benzema in line for moves as Al Hilal pursue Ollie Watkins

Darwin Nunez and Karim Benzema could both leave Al Hilal, with the Saudi Pro League giants eyeing up Ollie Watkins.

talkSPORT understands Al Hilal have tabled a £38million bid for Aston Villa and England striker Watkins.



2 Nunez joined Al Hilal from Liverpool 12 months ago Credit: Getty

Watkins, 30, scored 21 goals in all competitions for Villa last season and featured for England at this summer's World Cup.

His current contract at Villa runs until the summer of 2028.

Al Hilal's approach for Watkins comes after the record 21-time champions of Saudi Arabia held talks with Harry Kane's representative about an audacious swoop for the England captain.

However, it's expected Kane will commit his future to Bayern Munich by signing a new contract.



talkSPORT understands Al Hilal have also earmarked Galatasaray and Nigeria's Victor Osimhen as a potential centre-forward signing.

Former Liverpool frontman Nunez, 27, has endured a difficult time in Saudi Arabia.



Having joined Al Hilal from the Reds last summer, he found himself left out of their domestic league squad for the second half of the 2025/26 campaign due to a cap on the number of overseas players.

talkSPORT exclusively revealed on Monday that fellow Saudi Pro League side Diriyah Club were working on a loan move for Nunez.



He has also been linked with a switch to Turkish outfit Trabzonspor, who recently signed his old Liverpool teammate Mo Salah.

Nunez's omission from the Al Hilal squad came after the arrival of Benzema from fierce rivals Al Ittihad in February.

2 Benzema arrived in the Saudi Pro League in 2023 with Al Ittihad, doing the double in 2024/25 Credit: Getty

But while Real Madrid legend Benzema made a prolific impact for Al Hilal at the back end of 2025/26, scoring nine goals in 13 outings in all competitions, and has already opened his account this term, he might be on the move again.



Turning 39 in December, Benzema is in the twilight of his career, but he's shown with his output in recent months that he's lost little of that deadly striker's instinct – even if he is no longer playing in a top-five European league.

Al Hilal finished second in the Saudi Pro League last season behind Cristiano Ronaldo-captained Al Nassr.

Managed by ex-Inter Milan boss Simone Inzaghi, Al Hilal began the 2025/26 campaign with a 4-2 win over Al Faisaly.

Benzema opened the scoring with a penalty, with former Wolves midfielder Ruben Neves also converting twice from the spot.



Neves went on to bag another brace as Al Hilal beat Al Raed 2-0 in the King's Cup.

Sports.title: Hull City vs Manchester United LIVE commentary: Michael Carrick hints at return for player after 20 months
Sports.content:
Hull City vs Manchester United LIVE commentary: Michael Carrick hints at return for player after 20 months

Marcus Rashford could feature for Manchester United for the first time in 20 months in the opening lunchtime kick-off of the new Premier League season.

The Red Devils finished strongly last term with their former midfielder at the helm and start the 2026/27 campaign at newly promoted Hull City on Saturday.

4 Man United were the team to achieve the most points since Carrick was appointed as interim manager Credit: Getty

Carrick was awarded the permanent managerial role at Old Trafford after securing a third-place finish and qualifying for the Champions League.

During the transfer window, United have recruited strongly in their midfield with the additions of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

Additionally, Marcus Rashford could feature for United in the Premier League for the first time since December 2024, following loan spells with Aston Villa and Barcelona.

The 28-year-old, wearing the No. 9 jersey, logged his first minutes back in a United shirt in a 4-2 friendly defeat to Ruben Amorim's AC Milan last Saturday.

Carrick has consistently referred to the England international as 'our player' and admitted it was 'exciting' to have him back.

Meanwhile, the Tigers will be hoping to mark their top-flight return after a nine-year absence with a victory - though survival remains a daunting task for any newly promoted side.

Hull faced controversy last season to reach this position, beating Middlesbrough in the final after Southampton were caught cheating and banished from the play-off final after 'Spygate'.

Live commentary for Hull City vs Man United

The fixture will be played on Saturday, August 22.

It is scheduled to kick off at the MKM Stadium at 12:30pm.

talkSPORT will have live commentary of the match to open up the second day of the Premier League campaign.

4 Oli McBurnie scored 18 goals, and assisted eight for Hull in the Championship last season Credit: Getty

Coverage will begin on GameDay Exclusive at 11am, presented by Reshmin Chowdhury.

Commentary will come from Sam Matterface and former Hull manager and Manchester United defender Steve Bruce.

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app.

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

talkSPORT.com will also have all the action in our dedicated Premier League blog.

The match will be broadcast live on TNT Sports 1, with coverage also starting at 11am.

4 The MKM Stadium has not hosted a Premier League game since 2017 Credit: Getty

Team news for Hull City v Man United

United striker Benjamin Sesko trained at Carrington on Tuesday despite missing the entirety of United's pre-season schedule.

While the Slovenia international is expected to become the Red Devils main striker this season, Bryan Mbuemo, Matheus Cunha, and Joshua Zirkzee have all slotted in the position during pre-season.

Matthijs de Ligt was also present in training as he continues to step up his recovery ahead of the new campaign.

The Netherlands defender has been sidelined since last November with back surgery.

However, there were no signs of Mason Mount ahead of the season opener after the midfielder picked up a blow during a recent 1-1 draw against Paris Saint-Germain.

4 Sesko will hope to make a big impact this season after working hard over the summer on his return Credit: Getty

Speaking after the incident in Gothenburg, Carrick explained: "He got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him. We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful."

Between the posts, Senne Lammens remains the undisputed starter, with both Tom Heaton and Karl Darlow lacking match sharpness.

Meanwhile, Sergej Jakirovic has targeted strengthening the defence of the Tigers and has brought in Greece international keeper Konstantinos Tzolakis from Olympiacos and Senegalese centre-back Nobel Mendy from Rayo Vallecano.

Defenders Elliot Stroud and Lucas Herrington, alongside midfielders Hidemasa Morita and Jens Hjerto-Dahl, also look like quality additions to the squad.

Hull are expected to set up as a direct, counter-attacking unit built around supplying crosses to main target man Oli McBurnie.

Carrick says Man United 'are ready'

Carrick believes his team are heading into the new Premier League season in a positive mood despite ending pre-season with a 4-2 defeat to Milan.

He said: "I think, as a whole, it’s been very good, I think there are a lot of positives to take from it. A lot of the performances, the group’s grown and got stronger.

"So overall, I think [it’s been positive] barring today. We’re disappointed with today. We didn’t play well today, so there are reasons for that. We need to learn from it. We need to improve.

"On the whole, we’re ready for [Hull]. A lot of the boys will be better for the minutes and, as I say, we’ve done a lot of work on the training pitch.

"We’ve got a good squad, so there are decisions to be made.We’ve got a good week’s training this week as well to get some more work in. So we’ll be ready for next week.

"I think there’s a whole different feeling when it’s the first league game of the season. Having a whole squad back home, back at Carrington, and looking forward to the start."

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal closing in on Konsa, Man United in advanced talks for Baleba, Aston Villa announce double signing
Sports.content:
'I don't think he plays'

Danny Murphy thinks Ezri Konsa will be a 'great addition' for Arsenal, but he has some worries over his minutes in the future.

Murphy can't see the England centre-back starting once William Saliba is back from his injury later this season.

He told talkSPORT's White and Jordan: "He's a fantastic player, he's been great for Villa, so I understand the admiration from Arsenal.

"It's a step up in terms of trying to win trophies, but when everyone's fit, I don't think he plays ahead of Saliba or Gabriel.

"Most players trust themselves to get into a team and I'm sure he believes in himself, but the reality is, when Saliba gets back and the partnership he has with Gabriel, he's going to be playing in the lesser games.

"Arsenal's strength in depth is very impressive, but Konsa will be a great addition, he's a super player."

Murphy is also concerned about Aston Villa, who are now looking set to be left without one of their defenders ahead of the opening game of the Premier League season this weekend.

"If they get him, they've got a really accomplished and confident player," he said. "I'm surprised Villa are letting it happen.

"It leaves a gaping hole for Villa."

Sports.title: Manchester United close in on Carlos Baleba as Red Devils eye cut-price deal just one year after £115m price tag
Sports.content:
Manchester United close in on Carlos Baleba as Red Devils eye cut-price deal just one year after £115m price tag

Manchester United are in advanced talks to sign Carlos Baleba from Brighton, talkSPORT understands.

The Red Devils are confident of agreeing a deal for less than £75million.

2 The Cameroon international has been with Brighton since August 2023 Credit: Getty

Baleba has already agreed personal terms wit the Red Devils.

Has Manchester United previously gone after Carlos Baleba?

The 22-year-old was heavily courted by the Red Devils last season but a deal never came to fruition as Brighton took a hard line stance on keeping the midfielder at the club, valuing him at around £115million.

Once it became clear he would not move to Old Trafford, Baleba endured a dip in performances.

The Cameroon international was taken off at half-time in three of Brighton's opening seven Premier League fixtures last term.

In response to Baleba's worrying displays, Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler conceded there was a chance the 22-year-old had been affected by United's interest.

"For sure, when a young boy reads there is interest from Manchester United with a big, big offer, it might affect him deep, deep down,” Hurzeler said.

“That’s also part of the development to understand that when you play well, there comes a big offer, there comes a big club who wants to have him.

“But then to keep pushing, to be humble, stay here in Brighton, and try to make the next step with the team and that’s something we have to keep on working with him.

“I can’t give you a clear answer if it’s really affected him or not. But for sure, he’s a young boy and we need to understand he’s not a machine that if you click on then he always runs and off then he stops.

“We need to understand his feelings, his emotions, where he comes from, and that’s our responsibility."

2 Carrick is eyeing Baleba as another option to strengthen United's midfield Credit: Getty

Which other clubs are interested in Carlos Baleba?

Although United may be the front-runners for Baleba, they are not alone in the race for his signature.

talkSPORT understands Baleba is on Newcastle's radar as an option to replace Bruno Guimaraes.

The Magpies have a serious void in the heart of their midfield following Guimaraes' move to Arsenal.

However, Baleba is far from Newcastle's only midfield target, with Manchester City's Nico Gonzalez also on the shortlist.

Which players have Manchester United signed this summer?

The potential addition of Baleba continues United's midfield overhaul this summer.

Youri Tielemans joined from Aston Villa after the Red Devils triggered his £35m release clause while Andrey Santos arrived from Chelsea for £50m.

United also have Kobbie Mainoo in their midfield ranks, with the England international penning a new deal until 2031 in April.

Sports.title: Ethan Nwaneri ‘could be a massive hit’ if he moves to surprise Europa League club
Sports.content:
Ethan Nwaneri ‘could be a massive hit’ if he moves to surprise Europa League club

Ethan Nwaneri could light up the Bundesliga with a move to Bayer Leverkusen as the race to sign him hots up.

talkSPORT revealed last weekend that the Arsenal star is expected to leave the Gunners before the end of the transfer window.

5 Bayer Leverkusen have been named as an ideal landing spot for Nwaneri Credit: Getty

Nwaneri was left out by Mikel Arteta in his 20-man squad for the 3-0 Community Shield win against Manchester City on Sunday.

The club's academy graduate made just four starts across 12 appearances for Arsenal in the first half of last season after falling out of favour.

Just 12 months earlier, Nwaneri was drawing comparisons to England star Jude Bellingham and Spain's talisman, Lamine Yamal.

talkSPORT's Adrian Durham even went so far as to say it is a 'sackable offence' for Thomas Tuchel not to pick the teenager in his first England squad in March 2025.

The 19-year-old became the youngest player in Premier League history upon making his first-team debut against Brentford in 2022 aged 15 years and 181 days.

It was hoped that a loan move to Marseille in January to work under Roberto De Zerbi would reignite his development.

Ethan Nwaneri at Marseille

Nwaneri duly scored just 13 minutes into his debut, yet he found himself out of the team when De Zerbi - now the Tottenham boss - left the club.

Arsenal's No.22 was then an unused sub in five of Marseille's final six Ligue 1 games last season as the loan spell came to a sorry conclusion.

European football expert Andy Brassell explained to talkSPORT.com: "I can understand all the reasoning for Arteta sending him out to Marseille last season. And De Zerbi spent the first half of last season talking about how he wanted his number 10 to build around.

5 Nwaneri made just four appearances under De Zerbi Credit: Getty

"Clearly Arsenal loaned him to Marseille with the understanding that it was for De Zerbi. And De Zerbi would be the guy to develop him and have new and fresh ideas, and work with him and bring him on and give him responsibility as the central part in the team.

"Of course, he could play on the right-hand side cutting in.

"He did a little bit play on the right-hand side cutting in, at least until De Zerbi went. But really the idea was for Mason Greenwood to keep his spot there and Nwaneri to be the number 10.

"And then there were a few little teething problems. And that became a massive problem once De Zerbi went.

"Of course, maybe this is easy to say in retrospect, but I said it at the time actually. If you're pitching the wagon to De Zerbi a little bit too much when it's clear that his position was a little bit unstable.

"There was a lot going on emotionally at Marseille. He could leave at any point. And that kind of left Nwaneri in a really difficult position."

5 Nwaneri scored twice and registered one assist in nine Ligue 1 appearances Credit: Getty

Nwaneri transfer latest

Nwaneri would have hoped to hit the ground running back at pre-season with Arsenal after training with the England squad in the United States ahead of the World Cup.

However, his future now looks unclear following his absence on Sunday, with the German league touted as a potential landing spot.

Brassell added: "Depending on what sort of position you're going to put him in, I think the Bundesliga would be a good spot for him.

"Before Borussia Dortmund made their last couple of signings, notably that of [Konstantinos] Karetsas, I would have seen him being a really good fit for Dortmund. But now they've gone out there, and they've signed Karetsas.

"Giannis Konstantelias is coming as well from PAOK. They're not going to have the spot for him."

5 Nwaneri registered six Premier League goal involvements in 2024/25 compared to zero last season

Nwaneri to Leverkusen?

"I wonder if Leverkusen could be a good spot for him because they're looking for a right-sided, left-footed player," he continued.

"Now, again, that's not Nwaneri as a number 10, but I think just because we've had it in our heads for a couple of years that he should be the ultimate or eventual [Martin] Odegaard replacement; It doesn't mean that's all he can do.

"And I think him acting as a sort of wide playmaker and especially one who can come inside and score goals; I think that would be really good."

Leverkusen already have a No.10 in their squad, which is where Nwaneri views his best position, having handed Florian Wirtz's shirt number to USA international Malik Tillman last season.

Yet Carles Martínez Novell's men, who will be playing in the Europa League this season, have a pre-existing relationship with Arteta's Arsenal, having sanctioned the £34.5m exit of Piero Hincapie.

The Gunners were also touted to have held discussions over a potential deal for Nwaneri's fellow Englishman, Jarell Quansah.

5 Quansah was named in England's World Cup squad after featuring 43 times for Leverkusen last term Credit: Getty

"Now, look, Leverkusen have got a lot of players in their squad, a lot of good players in their squad, so you'd have to battle for space," Brassell told talkSPORT. "There's no doubt about that. But they are looking for a player in that exact spot [on the right].

"They're hoping to do a deal to bring Moussa Diaby back. Of course, he's in Saudi at the moment - Because he's in Saudi, he's waiting for a significant payoff before he leaves. And his current club would like to whack that onto the fee for Leverkusen, which they're obviously not that happy with.

"But I feel that Nwaneri could be a massive hit in the Bundesliga. Stuttgart, again, I think would be a good destination for him.

"Again, financially a little bit more difficult to do, I think. And unless there's a move out of Stuttgart, maybe he doesn't go straight into the XI there. So that's a question mark.

"Maybe it needs to be a post-Jamie Leweling thing. But I think it'd be great under the coaching of Sebastian Hoeneß.

"Leverkusen seems like a really interesting spot for me. And maybe that's something that could open up."

Sports.title: Aston Villa braced for fourth Ollie Watkins bid from Saudi side, with player open to switch - as Newcastle offered former Chelsea forward Christopher Nkunku: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Aston Villa braced for fourth Ollie Watkins bid from Saudi side, with player open to switch - as Newcastle offered former Chelsea forward Christopher Nkunku: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Villa braced for another Watkins bid

Aston Villa anticipate a fourth bid from Al Hilal for striker Ollie Watkins. The England international is open to the move but so far Villa have rejected their advances and want to keep the 30-year-old.

Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins is understood to be open to a move to Saudi Arabia

The latest bid of £38m was rejected on Tuesday evening. Villa maintain interested in Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson and have confirmed the signings of Matteo Ruggeri and Zion Suzuki.

Left back Ruggeri, 24, joins from Atletico Madrid, while goalkeeper Suzuki, 23, arrives after two years in Italy with Parma.

Meanwhile, Rangers have signed right back Kosta Nedeljkovic from Villa.

The 20-year-old has moved to Ibrox on a season-long loan, with a £4m obligation to buy, which will be triggered by the number of games he plays.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed last week, Villa are signing Aaron Wan Bissaka on loan from West Ham pending his medical today.

The deal can become an obligation to buy at around £18million.

Toon's Nkunku offer

Newcastle have been offered the chance to sign former Chelsea forward Christopher Nkunku from AC Milan.

However, their priority remains to sign a midfielder first hence talks with Man City for Nico Gonzalez. Other targets are also being discussed.

Nkunku has been told he can leave Milan and has interest from RB Leipzig among others.

Konsa nearing Arsenal move

Arsenal and Aston Villa are closing on agreement for Ezri Konsa.

Daily Mail Sport revealed last week that Arsenal had improved their offer to £40m plus add ons and talks were ongoing as they try to reach a compromise.

Read the full story here.

Baleba close to United switch

Manchester United are closing on a £65million deal for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba.

Talks resumed for the Cameroon international in recent weeks after it became apparent his ankle ligament injury was not as serious as first feared.

Read the full story here.

Pogba tears up Monaco deal

Monaco have confirmed that Paul Pogba has left by mutual agreement, bringing his time at the Ligue 1 club to a premature end.

The 33-year-old former Manchester United midfielder is now a free agent and has been offered to clubs in the MLS.

Read the full story here.

Paul Pogba's time at Monaco is over - with MLS clubs now considering a move for the former Man United midfielder

Farke reunites with Elvedi

Leeds have signed Nico Elvedi from Borussia Monchengladbach. The final fee is £6.5m rising to £8.5m with bonuses.

The 29-year-old Switzerland international centre back worked with Daniel Farke previously at the Bundesliga club.

James set for Wolves move

Rennes midfielder Jordan James is poised to finalise his move to Wolves today pending his medical.

The Wales international midfielder is joining on an initial loan deal with an option to sign permanently for around £10m.

He impressed on loan at Leicester last season scoring 11 goals in 34 games and had interest from Middlesbrough and West Ham.

Chelsea defender closes on Italy move

Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile has arrived at Villa Stuart in Rome ahead of his medical this morning.

The 25-year-old centre back is joining Napoli on loan for around £2.5m with an option for the deal to become permanent at £23m.

Mamadou Sarr, meanwhile, is emerging as a target for Real Sociedad and Al Hilal.

The 20-year-old has been expected to go on loan in the Premier League and interest there remains.

The Senegal international was recalled from a loan at Strasbourg to provide cover last season and started in their FA Cup win over Hull.

Piroe party at West Ham

West Ham have signed Joel Piroe on loan from Leeds until the end of the season.

The deal also includes an option for it to become permanent, which will be activated should certain conditions be met, including West Ham winning promotion back to the Premier League.

Joel Piroe has joined West Ham on loan from Leeds

West Ham turned to 27-year-old Piroe after hitting an impasse in talks for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott who is joining Real Betis for £17m plus add ons.

Piroe, who has scored 73 goals in the Championship during spells with Leeds and Swansea , said: 'I see West Ham as a Club that really wants to be in the Premier League, and I think should be in the Premier League.

'With my experience, I think I can help the Club a lot to achieve what they want to achieve, and I think it’s a good opportunity for me to show what I’ve learnt and how I’ve grown as a football player over the years.'

Piroe finished the 2024-25 season as the Championship's top scorer, helping Leeds United earn promotion to the Premier League.

The Hammers remain an option for free agent Jamie Vardy.

Potters snare Ipswich pair

Stoke have agreed a fee of around £6million with Ipswich for striker George Hirst and are also taking Ipswich full back Ben Johnson on loan.

Scotland international Hirst is to undergo medical later today. The fee will increase on performance related bonuses.
